Moreover, if taking what he gave her is not lawful for him, then what is other than it is forbidden to him all the more. It has been said that the address in His saying ﴿And it is not lawful for you﴾ is to the leaders and judges, to match His saying ﴿But if you fear﴾, for the address there is to the leaders and judges; and according to this, the attribution of the taking to them is because they are the ones who command it.

The first is preferable, because of His saying ﴿of what you have given them﴾, for attributing it to others than the husbands is very far-fetched, since the giving by husbands was not by their command. It has been said that the second is preferable so that the structure is not disturbed.

His saying ﴿except when they both fear﴾: that is, it is not permitted for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when they both fear ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, that is, the non-observance of the limits of Allah which He set for the spouses, and obligated them to fulfil, of good companionship and obedience. If they both fear that, ﴿then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up to be released﴾: that is, there is no blame upon the man in taking, nor upon the woman in giving, by her ransoming herself from that marriage by paying some property with which the husband is satisfied, so he divorces her on account of it. This is khul' (divorce by compensation), and the majority have gone to the permissibility of this for the husband, and that it is lawful for him to take with that fear; and this is what the Qur'an explicitly states.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from some scholars that it is not lawful for him to keep what he took, and he is not compelled to return it; and this is extremely weak.

Hamzah recited ﴿illa an yukhafa﴾ in the passive voice, with the agent omitted, namely the leaders and judges; Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, saying: because of His saying ﴿But if you fear﴾, so He made the fear belong to other than the spouses.

Those who made khul' subject to the authority (sultan) argued by this, and they are Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin.

An-Nahhas criticized the preference of Abu 'Ubayd mentioned above.

His saying ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾: that is, if the leaders and judges, or the intermediaries between the spouses even if they are not leaders and judges, fear the non-observance of the limits of Allah by the spouses, which are what He obligated upon them as has preceded.

It has been reported from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani that this verse is abrogated by His saying in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount, do not take from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ [an-Nisa' 20]. This is a view outside the consensus, and there is no contradiction between the two.

The scholars have differed: if the husband asks the wife for an increase over what he gave her of the dower and its associated items, and the wife agrees to that, is it permissible or not? The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is permissibility, since it is not restricted to a specific amount; and Malik, al-Shafi'i and Abu Thawr said this, and something similar has been related from a group of the Companions and the Successors. Tawus, 'Ata', al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq said that it is not permissible; and what has come concerning that from the Prophet ﷺ will come later.

His exalted saying ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: that is, the rulings of marriage and separation mentioned are the limits of Allah which you were commanded to follow, so do not transgress them by opposing them, lest you deserve what Allah mentioned of the censure upon the doer of that, that he is a wrongdoer.

His exalted saying ﴿And if he divorces her﴾: that is, the third pronouncement which He mentioned by His saying ﴿or release with kindness﴾; that is, if that occurs from him, then she has become forbidden to him by the triple divorce, ﴿then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾: that is, until she marries another husband.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and those who agreed with him took the apparent meaning of the verse, saying: mere contract suffices, since that is what is meant by His saying ﴿until she marries another husband﴾. The majority of the early and later scholars went to the view that intercourse is required along with the contract, because of what was established from the Prophet ﷺ requiring this, and it is an addition that must be accepted; and perhaps it did not reach Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and those who followed him. In the verse there is evidence that it must be a legitimate marriage intended for its own sake, not a marriage not intended for its own sake, but a mere device for halala (legitimizing return) and a means of returning her to the first husband; for that is forbidden, due to the texts reported condemning it and condemning its doer, and that he is the borrowed ram (al-tays al-musta'ar) whom the Lawgiver cursed, and cursed whoever takes him for that purpose.

His saying ﴿And if he divorces her﴾: that is, the second husband; ﴿then there is no blame upon them both﴾: that is, upon the first husband and the woman; ﴿for them to return to one another﴾: that is, each of them returns to the other.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: The scholars have agreed that if a free man divorces his wife three times, then her waiting period ends, she marries another husband, he consummates with her, then he separates from her and her waiting period ends, then the first husband marries her again, she is with him on three pronouncements.

His saying ﴿if they both think that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾: that is, the rights of marriage obligatory for each of them upon the other.

As for when that assumption does not arise, by their knowing or one of them knowing the non-observance of the limits of Allah, or they or one of them hesitate and the assumption does not arise for them, then entering this marriage is not permitted, since it is a likely cause of disobedience to Allah and falling into what He has forbidden to the spouses.

His saying ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾ refers to the rulings mentioned, as has preceded. He specified "those who know" although the call is general to the learned and others, and conveying is obligatory for every individual, because they are the ones who benefit from the explanation mentioned.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan have related from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: A man, when he divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period ended, that was his right, even if he divorced her a thousand times. A man deliberately divorced his wife, and when the time of the end of her waiting period drew near he took her back, then he divorced her again, then said: "By Allah, I will not shelter you with me, nor will you ever be lawful." So Allah revealed: ﴿The divorce is twice; then either retain in an honourable manner or release with kindness﴾, and from that day people began the divorce afresh, whether or not they had divorced.

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim related something similar and he authenticated it, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah.

al-Bukhari related from her: that a woman came to her and asked her about something of divorce. She said: I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ﴿The divorce is twice﴾ was revealed.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Abu Razin al-Asadi who said: "A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of Allah's saying ﴿The divorce is twice﴾; then where is the third? He said: The release with kindness is the third."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related something similar from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet.

'Abd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid that he said: Allah said to the third: ﴿then either retain in an honourable manner or release with kindness﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Yazid ibn Abi Habib who said: "Release" (tasrih) in the Book of Allah means divorce.

al-Bayhaqi related through al-Suddi from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and some Companions of the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying ﴿The divorce is twice﴾: they said: it is the appointed time in which return is possible; so when he divorces once or twice, either he retains and returns in an honourable manner, or he leaves her alone until her waiting period ends, whereupon she is more entitled to herself.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: A man used to eat from the property of his wife, which he had given her as a gift and other than it, not seeing any blame upon himself. So Allah revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, and after this verse it was no longer valid for them to take anything of their wealth except by right. Then He said: ﴿except when they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿But if they give you willingly of it, something of it, then consume it with enjoyment and satisfaction﴾ [an-Nisa' 4].

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿except when they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾: he said: except when the disobedience and bad conduct come from her side, so that she asks you to ransom herself from you, then there is no blame upon you for what she gives up to be released.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi related through 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn As'ad ibn Zurarah, from Habibah bint Sahl al-Ansari: "that she loved Thabit ibn Qays, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out for the dawn prayer and found her at his door in the darkness, and he said: Who is this? She said: I am Habibah bint Sahl. He said: What is your matter? She said: Neither I nor Thabit... When Thabit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: This is Habibah bint Sahl, and she mentioned what Allah willed her to mention. Habibah said: O Messenger of Allah, all that he gave me is with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Take from her. So he took from her, and she sat in her family's house."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and Habibah, for she had complained of him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Will you return to him his garden? She said: Yes. He summoned him and mentioned that to him. He said: Would that be good for me? He said: Yes. Thabit said: I have done it. So the verse was revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take...﴾, the verse."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi related through 'Amrah from 'A'ishah something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that "Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Salul, the wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays for his character or his religion, but I cannot bear him out of hatred, and I dislike disbelief in Islam. He said: Will you return to him his garden? She said: Yes. He said: Accept the garden and divorce her with a single divorce."

The wording of Ibn Majah: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to take back from her his garden and not to take more."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated through 'Ata' who said: "A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: I hate my husband and I love to be separated from him. He said: Will you return to him the garden that he gave you as a dowry? She said: Yes, and more. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: As for the more from your own property, no."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu al-Zubayr that Thabit ibn Qays mentioned the story, and in it: "As for the more, no."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a sound chain from Ibn 'Abbas, and in it: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded Thabit to take what he had given (p-155) and not to take more."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Sa'id, mentioning the story, and in it: "So she returned to him his garden and added to it."

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Umar that he said, concerning some women who sought khul': "Separate from him even for her earring."

In a wording narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq from him, he said to the husband: "Take even her hair braids."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Uthman permitted khul' except for her hair braids.

'Abd ibn Humayd and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Ata' that "the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked that a husband take from the woman who seeks khul' more than what he had given her."

Hadiths have come condemning women who seek khul', among them from Thawban in Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) and al-Bayhaqi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her." And he said: "The women who seek khul' are the hypocrites."

Among them, from Ibn 'Abbas in Ibn Majah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A woman should not ask her husband for divorce without a reason, for she will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance is detectable from a distance of forty years."

Among them, from Abu Hurayrah in Ahmad and al-Nasa'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Those who seek khul' and those who seek to be extracted are the hypocrites." Among them, from 'Uqbah in Ibn Jarir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

The scholars have differed concerning the waiting period ('iddah) of the woman who obtains khul'. The preponderant view is that she observes one menstrual cycle (hayd), based on what Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, and al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to observe one menstrual cycle."

And based on what al-Tirmidhi narrated from al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra': "She obtained khul' in the time of the Messenger of Allah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded her to observe one menstrual cycle, or it was commanded that she observe one menstrual cycle."

Al-Tirmidhi said: The sound view is that she was commanded to observe one menstrual cycle.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from her (ʿĀʾisha) that she said: "I obtained khul' from my husband, and I came to 'Uthman and asked him what waiting period was due from me. He said: There is no waiting period due from you, unless it is that you are newly with him, so you remain until you menstruate once. She said: I only follow in this the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning Maryam al-Mughaliyah, who loved Thabit ibn Qays and obtained khul' from him."

Al-Nasa'i narrated from al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh that "the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to wait one menstrual cycle and then join her family."

Nothing opposes this among the raised (marfu') reports. Rather, it has been reported from a group of the Companions and the Successors that the waiting period of the woman who obtains khul' is like the waiting period of divorce, and this is the view of the majority.

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is the view of most scholars among the Companions and others, and they argued for it on the basis that the woman who obtains khul' is among the divorced women, so she falls under the general scope of the Qur'an.

The truth is what we have mentioned, because what has been reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) specifies the general scope of the Qur'an.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him﴾ that he said: If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ali something similar.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatadah something similar.

Al-Shafi'i, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Aishah, who said: "The wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: I was with Rifa'ah and he divorced me with a final divorce, so 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr married me, but with him is nothing except like the fringe of a garment. The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled and said: Do you wish to return to Rifa'ah? No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes yours."

Something similar to this has been narrated from her through several chains.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar also.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. These three Companions did not name the woman of the story.

Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that "al-'Umaysa' or al-Rumaysa' came to the Prophet (ﷺ)," and at its end the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That is not for you until another man tastes your sweetness."

The curse upon the muhallil (the one who marries a woman to make her lawful to her former husband) has been established in hadiths, among them from Ibn Mas'ud in Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sahih), al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) cursed the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil."

Among them, from 'Ali in Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. Among them, from Jabir traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in al-Tirmidhi, similar. Among them, from Ibn 'Abbas traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Ibn Majah, similar. Among them, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir in Ibn Majah, al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) and al-Bayhaqi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar. Among them, from Abu Hurayrah traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi, similar.

There are hadiths in the chapter condemning tahlil and the one who performs it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿Then if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them both if they return to each other﴾ that he said: If she marries after the first and the second husband consummates the marriage with her, then there is no blame upon the first if he marries her when the other divorces her or dies leaving her, for she has then become lawful to him.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muqatil concerning His words ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾ that he said: the command of Allah and His obedience.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verse 229–230 (part 1 of 2):

The divorce mentioned here is the revocable divorce, as is shown by what preceded in the first verse. That is, the divorce in which the husbands have the right of return (raj'ah) is "two times," meaning the first and second pronouncement, since there is no return after the third. Almighty Allah said "two times" and did not say "two pronouncements" to indicate that divorce should be one time after another, not two pronouncements at once; so said a group of the exegetes. Since after the second pronouncement there remain only one of two matters, either pronouncing the third, by which the wife becomes irrevocably separated (tabin), or retaining her and continuing the marriage, and not pronouncing the third upon her, Almighty Allah said: ﴿Then either retain them in an honourable manner or release them with kindness﴾. That is: then either retention after return for one who has been divorced by her husband twice, in an honourable manner, meaning in what is recognized as good by people in good companionship; ﴿or release with kindness﴾, meaning by pronouncing a third pronouncement upon her without harming her. It has been said that the meaning is: ﴿then retain in an honourable manner﴾, meaning by return after the second pronouncement; ﴿or release with kindness﴾, meaning by leaving off return after the second until her waiting period (iddah) ends.

The first is more apparent.

His saying ﴿The divorce﴾ is a subject with an omitted modifier: that is, the number of divorces in which return is established is two times.

The scholars have differed concerning the pronouncing of three at once in a single utterance: does it take effect as three or as one only? The majority went to the first, and those other than them went to the second, which is the truth.

I have established this in my writings with thorough proof, and devoted a separate treatise to it.

His saying ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾: the address is to the husbands. That is, it is not lawful for husbands to take anything of the dower that they gave to their wives, in a manner of harm to them. The indefinite "anything" (shay'an) is for belittling: that is, anything trivial, let alone much. He specified what they gave them with the prohibition of taking from it, although it is not lawful for husbands to take any of their wealth that they own apart from the dower, because that is what the husband's soul is attached to and longs to take, to the exclusion of others, of what is in her possession. Moreover, if taking what he gave her is not lawful for him, then what is other than it is forbidden to him all the more. It has been said that the address in His saying ﴿And it is not lawful for you﴾ is to the leaders and judges, to match His saying ﴿But if you fear﴾, for the address there is to the leaders and judges; and according to this, the attribution of the taking to them is because they are the ones who command it.

The first is preferable, because of His saying ﴿of what you have given them﴾, for attributing it to others than the husbands is very far-fetched, since the giving by husbands was not by their command. It has been said that the second is preferable so that the structure is not disturbed.

His saying ﴿except when they both fear﴾: that is, it is not permitted for you to take anything of what you have given them, except when they both fear ﴿that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, that is, the non-observance of the limits of Allah which He set for the spouses, and obligated them to fulfil, of good companionship and obedience. If they both fear that, ﴿then there is no blame upon them for what she gives up to be released﴾: that is, there is no blame upon the man in taking, nor upon the woman in giving, by her ransoming herself from that marriage by paying some property with which the husband is satisfied, so he divorces her on account of it. This is khul' (divorce by compensation), and the majority have gone to the permissibility of this for the husband, and that it is lawful for him to take with that fear; and this is what the Qur'an explicitly states.

Ibn al-Mundhir related from some scholars that it is not lawful for him to keep what he took, and he is not compelled to return it; and this is extremely weak.

Hamzah recited ﴿illa an yukhafa﴾ in the passive voice, with the agent omitted, namely the leaders and judges; Abu 'Ubayd preferred this, saying: because of His saying ﴿But if you fear﴾, so He made the fear belong to other than the spouses.

Those who made khul' subject to the authority (sultan) argued by this, and they are Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin.

An-Nahhas criticized the preference of Abu 'Ubayd mentioned above.

His saying ﴿But if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾: that is, if the leaders and judges, or the intermediaries between the spouses even if they are not leaders and judges, fear the non-observance of the limits of Allah by the spouses, which are what He obligated upon them as has preceded.

It has been reported from Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Muzani that this verse is abrogated by His saying in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount, do not take from it anything. Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ [an-Nisa' 20]. This is a view outside the consensus, and there is no contradiction between the two.

The scholars have differed: if the husband asks the wife for an increase over what he gave her of the dower and its associated items, and the wife agrees to that, is it permissible or not? The apparent meaning of the Qur'an is permissibility, since it is not restricted to a specific amount; and Malik, al-Shafi'i and Abu Thawr said this, and something similar has been related from a group of the Companions and the Successors. Tawus, 'Ata', al-Awza'i, Ahmad and Ishaq said that it is not permissible; and what has come concerning that from the Prophet ﷺ will come later.

His exalted saying ﴿These are the limits of Allah﴾: that is, the rulings of marriage and separation mentioned are the limits of Allah which you were commanded to follow, so do not transgress them by opposing them, lest you deserve what Allah mentioned of the censure upon the doer of that, that he is a wrongdoer.

His exalted saying ﴿And if he divorces her﴾: that is, the third pronouncement which He mentioned by His saying ﴿or release with kindness﴾; that is, if that occurs from him, then she has become forbidden to him by the triple divorce, ﴿then she is not lawful to him after that until she marries another husband﴾: that is, until she marries another husband.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and those who agreed with him took the apparent meaning of the verse, saying: mere contract suffices, since that is what is meant by His saying ﴿until she marries another husband﴾. The majority of the early and later scholars went to the view that intercourse is required along with the contract, because of what was established from the Prophet ﷺ requiring this, and it is an addition that must be accepted; and perhaps it did not reach Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and those who followed him. In the verse there is evidence that it must be a legitimate marriage intended for its own sake, not a marriage not intended for its own sake, but a mere device for halala (legitimizing return) and a means of returning her to the first husband; for that is forbidden, due to the texts reported condemning it and condemning its doer, and that he is the borrowed ram (al-tays al-musta'ar) whom the Lawgiver cursed, and cursed whoever takes him for that purpose.

His saying ﴿And if he divorces her﴾: that is, the second husband; ﴿then there is no blame upon them both﴾: that is, upon the first husband and the woman; ﴿for them to return to one another﴾: that is, each of them returns to the other.

Ibn al-Mundhir said: The scholars have agreed that if a free man divorces his wife three times, then her waiting period ends, she marries another husband, he consummates with her, then he separates from her and her waiting period ends, then the first husband marries her again, she is with him on three pronouncements.

His saying ﴿if they both think that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾: that is, the rights of marriage obligatory for each of them upon the other.

As for when that assumption does not arise, by their knowing or one of them knowing the non-observance of the limits of Allah, or they or one of them hesitate and the assumption does not arise for them, then entering this marriage is not permitted, since it is a likely cause of disobedience to Allah and falling into what He has forbidden to the spouses.

His saying ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾ refers to the rulings mentioned, as has preceded. He specified "those who know" although the call is general to the learned and others, and conveying is obligatory for every individual, because they are the ones who benefit from the explanation mentioned.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan have related from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: A man, when he divorced his wife and then took her back before her waiting period ended, that was his right, even if he divorced her a thousand times. A man deliberately divorced his wife, and when the time of the end of her waiting period drew near he took her back, then he divorced her again, then said: "By Allah, I will not shelter you with me, nor will you ever be lawful." So Allah revealed: ﴿The divorce is twice; then either retain in an honourable manner or release with kindness﴾, and from that day people began the divorce afresh, whether or not they had divorced.

At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Mardawayh, al-Hakim related something similar and he authenticated it, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah.

al-Bukhari related from her: that a woman came to her and asked her about something of divorce. She said: I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and ﴿The divorce is twice﴾ was revealed.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related from Abu Razin al-Asadi who said: "A man said: O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of Allah's saying ﴿The divorce is twice﴾; then where is the third? He said: The release with kindness is the third."

Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi related something similar from Ibn 'Abbas, traced to the Prophet.

'Abd ibn Humayd related from Mujahid that he said: Allah said to the third: ﴿then either retain in an honourable manner or release with kindness﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Yazid ibn Abi Habib who said: "Release" (tasrih) in the Book of Allah means divorce.

al-Bayhaqi related through al-Suddi from Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and some Companions of the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying ﴿The divorce is twice﴾: they said: it is the appointed time in which return is possible; so when he divorces once or twice, either he retains and returns in an honourable manner, or he leaves her alone until her waiting period ends, whereupon she is more entitled to herself.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas who said: A man used to eat from the property of his wife, which he had given her as a gift and other than it, not seeing any blame upon himself. So Allah revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them﴾, and after this verse it was no longer valid for them to take anything of their wealth except by right. Then He said: ﴿except when they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah. And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾, and He said: ﴿But if they give you willingly of it, something of it, then consume it with enjoyment and satisfaction﴾ [an-Nisa' 4].

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿except when they both fear that they will not keep within the limits of Allah﴾: he said: except when the disobedience and bad conduct come from her side, so that she asks you to ransom herself from you, then there is no blame upon you for what she gives up to be released.

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi related through 'Amrah bint 'Abd al-Rahman ibn As'ad ibn Zurarah, from Habibah bint Sahl al-Ansari: "that she loved Thabit ibn Qays, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out for the dawn prayer and found her at his door in the darkness, and he said: Who is this? She said: I am Habibah bint Sahl. He said: What is your matter? She said: Neither I nor Thabit... When Thabit ibn Qays came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: This is Habibah bint Sahl, and she mentioned what Allah willed her to mention. Habibah said: O Messenger of Allah, all that he gave me is with him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Take from her. So he took from her, and she sat in her family's house."

Ibn Jarir related from Ibn Jurayj who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Thabit ibn Qays and Habibah, for she had complained of him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: Will you return to him his garden? She said: Yes. He summoned him and mentioned that to him. He said: Would that be good for me? He said: Yes. Thabit said: I have done it. So the verse was revealed: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take...﴾, the verse."

'Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi related through 'Amrah from 'A'ishah something similar.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verses 229–230 (part 2 of 2):

Al-Bukhari, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that "Jamilah bint 'Abd Allah ibn Salul, the wife of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I do not blame Thabit ibn Qays for his character or his religion, but I cannot bear him out of hatred, and I dislike disbelief in Islam. He said: Will you return to him his garden? She said: Yes. He said: Accept the garden and divorce her with a single divorce."

The wording of Ibn Majah: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to take back from her his garden and not to take more."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated through 'Ata' who said: "A woman came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: I hate my husband and I love to be separated from him. He said: Will you return to him the garden that he gave you as a dowry? She said: Yes, and more. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: As for the more from your own property, no."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu al-Zubayr that Thabit ibn Qays mentioned the story, and in it: "As for the more, no."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated with a sound chain from Ibn 'Abbas, and in it: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded Thabit to take what he had given (p-155) and not to take more."

Al-Bayhaqi narrated from Abu Sa'id, mentioning the story, and in it: "So she returned to him his garden and added to it."

Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Umar that he said, concerning some women who sought khul': "Separate from him even for her earring."

In a wording narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq from him, he said to the husband: "Take even her hair braids."

Al-Bukhari said: 'Uthman permitted khul' except for her hair braids.

'Abd ibn Humayd and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Ata' that "the Prophet (ﷺ) disliked that a husband take from the woman who seeks khul' more than what he had given her."

Hadiths have come condemning women who seek khul', among them from Thawban in Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) and al-Bayhaqi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without any need, the fragrance of Paradise is forbidden to her." And he said: "The women who seek khul' are the hypocrites."

Among them, from Ibn 'Abbas in Ibn Majah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A woman should not ask her husband for divorce without a reason, for she will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, though its fragrance is detectable from a distance of forty years."

Among them, from Abu Hurayrah in Ahmad and al-Nasa'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Those who seek khul' and those who seek to be extracted are the hypocrites." Among them, from 'Uqbah in Ibn Jarir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.

The scholars have differed concerning the waiting period ('iddah) of the woman who obtains khul'. The preponderant view is that she observes one menstrual cycle (hayd), based on what Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, and al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to observe one menstrual cycle."

And based on what al-Tirmidhi narrated from al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh ibn 'Afra': "She obtained khul' in the time of the Messenger of Allah, and the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded her to observe one menstrual cycle, or it was commanded that she observe one menstrual cycle."

Al-Tirmidhi said: The sound view is that she was commanded to observe one menstrual cycle.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from her (ʿĀʾisha) that she said: "I obtained khul' from my husband, and I came to 'Uthman and asked him what waiting period was due from me. He said: There is no waiting period due from you, unless it is that you are newly with him, so you remain until you menstruate once. She said: I only follow in this the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning Maryam al-Mughaliyah, who loved Thabit ibn Qays and obtained khul' from him."

Al-Nasa'i narrated from al-Rubayyi' bint Mu'awwidh that "the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded the wife of Thabit ibn Qays to wait one menstrual cycle and then join her family."

Nothing opposes this among the raised (marfu') reports. Rather, it has been reported from a group of the Companions and the Successors that the waiting period of the woman who obtains khul' is like the waiting period of divorce, and this is the view of the majority.

Al-Tirmidhi said: This is the view of most scholars among the Companions and others, and they argued for it on the basis that the woman who obtains khul' is among the divorced women, so she falls under the general scope of the Qur'an.

The truth is what we have mentioned, because what has been reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) specifies the general scope of the Qur'an.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿Then if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him﴾ that he said: If he divorces her three times, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband.

Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from 'Ali something similar.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatadah something similar.

Al-Shafi'i, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Aishah, who said: "The wife of Rifa'ah al-Qurazi came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: I was with Rifa'ah and he divorced me with a final divorce, so 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Zubayr married me, but with him is nothing except like the fringe of a garment. The Prophet (ﷺ) smiled and said: Do you wish to return to Rifa'ah? No, not until you taste his sweetness and he tastes yours."

Something similar to this has been narrated from her through several chains.

'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar also.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar. These three Companions did not name the woman of the story.

Ahmad and al-Nasa'i narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that "al-'Umaysa' or al-Rumaysa' came to the Prophet (ﷺ)," and at its end the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "That is not for you until another man tastes your sweetness."

The curse upon the muhallil (the one who marries a woman to make her lawful to her former husband) has been established in hadiths, among them from Ibn Mas'ud in Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it sahih), al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) cursed the muhallil and the one for whom he is muhallil."

Among them, from 'Ali in Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and al-Bayhaqi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud. Among them, from Jabir traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in al-Tirmidhi, similar. Among them, from Ibn 'Abbas traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Ibn Majah, similar. Among them, from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir in Ibn Majah, al-Hakim (who graded it sahih) and al-Bayhaqi, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), similar. Among them, from Abu Hurayrah traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) in Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah and al-Bayhaqi, similar.

There are hadiths in the chapter condemning tahlil and the one who performs it.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿Then if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them both if they return to each other﴾ that he said: If she marries after the first and the second husband consummates the marriage with her, then there is no blame upon the first if he marries her when the other divorces her or dies leaving her, for she has then become lawful to him.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Muqatil concerning His words ﴿that they will keep within the limits of Allah﴾ that he said: the command of Allah and His obedience.

The meaning of "reaching" (al-bulugh) to something is literally arriving at it. It is used in the sense of "approaching" only metaphorically, through a connection together with a contextual indicator, as here. The literal meaning cannot be intended, because when the woman has reached the last part of the waiting period ('iddah) and passed beyond it to the part that is the term of its completion, she has already left the 'iddah, and the husband no longer has any authority over her.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: The meaning of *balaghna* ("they have reached") here is "they have approached," by the consensus (ijma') of the scholars.

He said: The meaning also necessitates this, because after the term has been reached he has no option to retain her, and retaining her "in good fashion" means fulfilling the rights of marriage. That is: when you divorce women and they approach the end of their 'iddah, do not harm them by taking them back without intending to resume the marriage and continue it. Rather, choose one of two matters: either retaining them in good fashion without intending harm, or releasing them with kindness, that is, leaving them until their 'iddah ends without taking them back to harm them. Do not retain them to harm them, as the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do, divorcing the woman until her 'iddah is about to end, then taking her back, not out of need nor out of love, but to prolong the 'iddah and extend the period of waiting, as harm, intending transgression against them and wronging them. ﴿And whoever does that has wronged himself﴾, because he has exposed himself to the punishment and wrath of Allah.

Al-Zajjaj said: That is, he has exposed himself to punishment, because doing what Allah has forbidden is an exposure to the punishment of Allah. ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾, that is, do not treat the rulings of Allah as a matter of mockery, for they are all serious; whoever jests with them, it binds him. He, glory be to Him, forbade them to do as the Jahiliyyah used to do, for a man among them would divorce, or manumit, or marry, and say, "I was only joking."

Al-Qurtubi said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that whoever divorces while jesting, the divorce binds him.

His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾, that is, the favour by which you came to be in Islam and its laws, after you had been in a state of utter ignorance and darknesses, one upon another. "The Book" is the Qur'an.

"The wisdom" (al-hikmah), the commentators said, is the sunnah which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established for them. ﴿He admonishes you thereby﴾, that is, He warns you with what He has sent down to you. He mentioned the Book and the wisdom separately, although they are included in the favour from the outset, to draw attention to their importance and great status.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man would divorce his wife, then take her back before her 'iddah ended, then divorce her again, doing this to harm her and keep her in suspension. So Allah revealed: ﴿And when you divorce women﴾ to the end of the verse.

Malik, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related something similar from Thawr ibn Yazid.

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi related from al-Hasan regarding His saying: ﴿And do not retain them to harm them, that you may transgress﴾, he said: It is the man who divorces his wife, and when she is about to complete her 'iddah he calls witnesses to her return, wanting to prolong it over her.

Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi related from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «What is the matter with people who play with the limits of Allah? One says, "I have divorced you, I have taken you back, I have divorced you, I have taken you back." This is not the divorce of the Muslims. Divorce the woman at the beginning of her 'iddah.»

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: «In the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a man would say to another man, "I have married you my daughter," then say, "I was only joking." He would say, "You have been freed," then say, "I was only joking." So Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, whoever says them in jest or not in jest, they are binding upon him: divorce, marriage, and manumission."»

Ibn Mardawayh related from Abu al-Darda', who said: «A man would divorce and then say, "I was playing," or free a slave and then say, "I was playing." So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever divorces or frees and says, 'I was playing,' his words are of no account; it takes effect upon him and binds him."»

Ibn Mardawayh also related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: «A man divorced his wife while playing, not intending divorce. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not take the verses of Allah in jest﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made the divorce binding upon him.»

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ), a report similar to the hadith of 'Ubadah.

Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, who graded it as hasan, Ibn Majah, and al-Hakim, who graded it as sahih, related from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «Three things, their seriousness is serious and their jest is serious: marriage, divorce, and taking back (the wife).»

The address in this verse, with His words ﴿When you divorce﴾ and His words ﴿do not prevent them﴾, may either be to the husbands, and the meaning of "prevention" (ʿadl) on their part is that they prevent the women from marrying the husbands they wish to marry after the completion of their waiting period (ʿidda), out of jahili zealotry, as frequently occurs among caliphs and sultans out of jealousy toward the women who were under them, lest they become under others. This is because, having attained worldly leadership and the arrogance and pride that come with it, they imagine that they have left the category of the children of Adam, except for those whom Allah protects among them through piety and humility. Or the address may be to the guardians (awliyaʾ), and the meaning of attributing the divorce to them is that they are the cause of it, since they are the ones who marry off the women to the husbands who divorced them.

The "term" (ajal) mentioned here is meant in its literal sense: that is, its end, not as in the first verse.

Al-ʿadl means "confinement" (al-habs).

Al-Khalil reported: "a hen that is muʿdila," meaning its egg has become stuck. It was also said that al-ʿadl is restriction and prevention, which goes back to the meaning of confinement. One says: "I wanted a matter and you prevented me from it (faʿadaltani ʿanhu), i.e. you hindered me and constrained me," and "the matter was made difficult (uʿdila)" when the stratagems are exhausted for you in it.

Al-Azhari said: the origin of al-ʿadl comes from their saying "the she-camel's young became stuck (ʿadalat al-nagatu)" when its offspring is lodged and its exit is not easy, and "the hen became stuck (ʿadalat al-dajajatu)" when its egg is lodged. Every difficult matter, in the view of the Arabs, is muʿdil. From this is the saying of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him:

"When difficult matters confront me, I uncover their hidden meaning by reflection."

One says aʿdala al-amru when it intensifies, and dāʾ ʿuḍāl means a severe illness, difficult to cure, which has defeated the physicians. ʿAdala fulan ayimahu means he prevented her (from remarrying). The forms yaʿḍuluhā with ḍamma and kasra are two dialects.

His words "that they marry" (an yankihna): its meaning is "from their marrying." Its position is in the genitive according to al-Khalil, and in the accusative according to Sibawayh and al-Farraʾ. It was also said that it is a substitute of inclusion (badal ishtimal) for the pronoun in the accusative in His words ﴿do not prevent them﴾.

His words "their husbands" (azwajahunna): if it is meant as those who had divorced them, then it is a metaphor by consideration of what was; if it is meant as those whom they wish to marry, then it is a metaphor by consideration of what will be.

His words "that" (dhalika) refer to the rulings that have been detailed. It is used in the singular, although the antecedent is plural, taking into account the meaning of plurality by interpreting it as "the group" and the like.

His words "that" (dhalikum) are construed with the plural form; He, glory be to Him, varied between the two demonstratives for stylistic variety (iftinan).

His words "purer" (azka) mean more increasing, more beneficial, and purer from defilements. ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾ what is good for you in it.

Al-Bukhari, the authors of the Sunan, and others have related from Maʿqil ibn Yasar, who said: "I had a sister, and a paternal cousin came to me, and I married her to him. She remained with him as long as she remained. Then he divorced her with one divorce, and did not take her back until her waiting period ended. Then he came to propose to her again along with the suitors. I said to him: 'You wretch! I honored you by her and married her to you, and you divorced her, then you came proposing to her! By Allah, she will never return to you.' He was a man with no fault, and the woman wished to return to him. So Allah knew his need for her and her need for her husband, and Allah revealed ﴿When you divorce women﴾ the verse." He said: "So I am the one about whom this verse was revealed; I expiated for my oath and married her to him."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning a man who divorces his wife with one or two divorces, and her waiting period ends; then it occurs to him to marry her again and take her back, and the woman wishes this, but her guardian prevented her from that, so Allah forbade them to prevent her."

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Suddi, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari. He had a paternal cousin whose husband divorced her with one divorce and her waiting period ended. He wanted to take her back, but Jabir refused and said: 'You divorced our paternal cousin, then you want to marry her again!' The woman wished to return to her husband, so Allah revealed ﴿When you divorce women﴾."

Ibn Abi Hatim related from Muqatil, regarding ﴿when they agree among themselves in a fair manner﴾, that it means with a dowry, a witness, and a new marriage contract.

Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh related from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Marry off the unmarried (al-ayama).' A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the ties (ʿalaʾiq) between them?' He said: 'What their families agree upon.'"

Ibn al-Mundhir related from al-Dahhak, who said regarding ﴿And Allah knows, while you do not know﴾: "Allah knows the love of each of the two for the other, which you, O guardian, do not know."

[Page 158 marker not translated]

When God, glorified is He, mentioned marriage and divorce, He mentioned nursing, because the spouses may separate while they have a child between them. For this reason it has been said that this ruling applies specifically to divorced women, and it has also been said that it is general.

His saying, ﴿Mothers shall nurse﴾, has been said to be a report with the meaning of a command, to indicate that its content is certain to occur. It has also been said to be a report in its own right, not carrying the meaning of a command, as explained earlier in His saying, ﴿shall wait﴾ [al-Baqarah: 228]. His saying, ﴿two full years﴾, is an emphasis to indicate that this period is a precise determination, not an approximate one.

His saying, ﴿for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾, means: this ruling is for whoever wishes to complete the nursing. It is evidence that nursing for two years is not obligatory but is the complete period, and that it is permissible to stop at less than that.

Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin recited ﴿for whoever wishes that it be completed﴾ with a fatha on the ta' and a raf' on al-rada'ah (nursing), attributing the verb to it.

Abu Haywah, Ibn Abi Ablah, and al-Jarud ibn Abi Sabrah recited al-ridā'ah (nursing) with a kasra on the ra', and this is a dialectal form.

It is narrated from Mujahid that he recited al-ri'dah. Ibn Abbas recited ﴿for whoever wishes to perfect the nursing﴾.

Al-Nahhas said: The Basrans do not know al-ridā'ah except with a fatha on the ra'.

The Kufans reported that the kasra is permissible.

The verse indicates that nursing is obligatory on the mother for her child, and this has been understood as applying when the infant will not accept any other.

His saying, ﴿And upon the one to whom the child belongs is their provision and their clothing﴾, means: upon the father to whom the child is born. He chose this wording instead of "upon the parent" to indicate that children belong to fathers, not to mothers, and for this reason they are attributed to them and not to the women, as if the women had given birth to them only. The meaning of this has been mentioned in al-Kashshaf. By provision here is meant adequate food customarily known among people, and by clothing is meant what they customarily provide. In this is evidence that fathers are obligated to provide this for nursing mothers.

This applies to divorced women. As for women who are not divorced, their maintenance and clothing are obligatory on their husbands, regardless of whether they nurse their children.

His saying, ﴿No soul is charged except according to its capacity﴾, is a restriction on His saying "in accordance with what is customary." That is: this maintenance and clothing that are obligatory on the father are to be provided according to what people customarily know, and he is charged only with what falls within his ability and capacity, not with what is burdensome to him or beyond him. It has also been said that the meaning is: the woman is not charged to endure stinginess in the wage, and the husband is not charged with extravagance, but moderation is observed.

His saying, ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾. Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and a group recited it with a raf' as a report, and Aban narrated it from Asim with a raf'. Nafi', Ibn Amir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Asim in the well-known transmission from him recited tudārra with a fatha on the doubled ra', as a prohibition. Its original form is lā tuḍārir or lā tuḍārar, in the active or passive voice. The meaning is: do not harm the father on account of the child, by demanding from him provision and clothing that he cannot afford, or by neglecting the child's protection and the care he needs. Or: the mother is not to be harmed by her husband, by his falling short in something that is obligatory on him, or by his taking the child from her without cause. The reading with a raf' admits both meanings. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited lā tuḍārar in its original form, with a fatha on the first ra'. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' recited lā tuḍār with a sukun on the ra' and no doubling, and it is also narrated from him with a sukun and doubling. al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas recited lā tuḍārir with a kasra on the first ra'. It is permissible for the ba' in His saying "through her child" to be connected to tuḍārru, on the understanding that it means taḍurru (to harm). That is: a mother should not harm her child by raising him badly or by neglecting his nourishment. The child is attributed sometimes to the father and sometimes to the mother, because each of them deserves to be named in relation to him, and this carries an appeal to compassion. This sentence elaborates on the preceding sentence and confirms it: neither of them should charge the other with what he cannot bear, so that neither harms the other on account of their child.

His saying, ﴿And upon the heir﴾, is coordinated with His saying, ﴿upon the one to whom the child belongs﴾, and what lies between them is an explanation of "in accordance with what is customary," or a parenthetical justification placed between the coordinated and the coordinated-to.

The scholars differed over the meaning of His saying, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾. It has been said that the heir is the child's heir: that is, if the one to whom the child belongs dies, the heir of this child is obligated to nurse him, as the father was obligated. This was said by Umar ibn al-Khattab, Qatadah, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ata, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Hanifah, and Ibn Abi Layla, with disagreement among them as to whether the obligation falls on whoever takes a share of the inheritance, or on males only, or on every relative in the womb-line even if he is not an heir. It has also been said that the heir here means the father's heir, on whom the nursing mother's maintenance and clothing are obligatory in accordance with what is customary. This was said by al-Dahhak.

Malik, in explaining this verse, said something like what al-Dahhak said, but he added that it is abrogated (mansukhah, i.e., its ruling has been canceled by a later ruling, naskh), and that a man is not obligated to maintain a brother, a relative, or a kinsman. Al-Dahhak made a condition that the child has no property; if the child has property, the wage for his nursing is taken from his property.

It has also been said that the heir mentioned in the verse is the child himself: that is, he is obligated to nurse himself from his own property if his father dies and he inherits from his property. This was said by Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb and Bashir ibn Nasir, the judge of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz. It is also narrated from al-Shafi'i. It has also been said that it refers to the surviving one of the child's two parents after the death of the other: when the father dies, the mother is responsible for the child's sustenance if he has no property. This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri.

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾, is that the heir of the nursing mother is obligated to treat the child as the mother used to treat him, with nursing, service, and upbringing.

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾, is that it is forbidden for him to harm the mother, just as it is forbidden for the father. A group of scholars held this view, and they said: this is the basic meaning, and whoever claims that the coordination refers back to all that was previously mentioned must provide evidence.

Al-Qurtubi said: This is the correct view, for if He had meant the whole of it, that is nursing, support, and not harming, it would be said "upon the heir are the like of these." So this shows that it is coordinated with the prohibition on harm. On this interpretation, as reported by Qadi Abd al-Wahhab, all the exegetes agreed.

Ibn Atiyyah said: Malik, all his companions, al-Sha'bi, al-Zuhri, al-Dahhak, and a group of scholars said: what is meant by His saying "the like of that" is that he must not harm. As for provision and clothing, nothing of them is obligatory.

Ibn al-Qasim reported from Malik something like what we mentioned earlier about his interpretation of this verse, and the claim of abrogation.

The weakness of what this group has adopted is not hidden from you. The meaning they restricted His saying, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾, to, namely the absence of harm to the nursing mother, has already been conveyed by His saying, ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾, since that applies to every act of harm coming to her from the one to whom the child belongs or from anyone else.

As for al-Qurtubi's statement, that if He had meant the whole He would have said "the like of these," the weakness in it is clear, for the demonstrative can refer to the plural as well as to the singular, by interpreting it as referring to what was mentioned or something similar.

As for the view of the first group, that the heir means the child's heir, it may be objected: if he is not a real heir while the child is alive, then he is an heir only figuratively, in terms of what he will become.

As for the view of the second group, although it takes the heir in its literal sense, there is a problem in making maintenance obligatory on him while the child is wealthy. For this reason the proponent of that view restricted it to the case where the child is poor. The reason for the difference in interpreting "heir" is what was mentioned earlier concerning the mention of the mothers, the one to whom the child belongs, and the father. So it is possible that "heir" is attributed to each of them.

His saying, ﴿But if they both desire weaning﴾: the pronoun refers to the two parents.

Fisal is weaning from nursing, that is, separating the child from the breast. From it the young camel (fasil) is named, because it is separated from its mother.

His saying, ﴿by mutual consent between them﴾ means: proceeding from mutual consent of the two parents, when the weaning takes place before the two years. ﴿There is no blame upon them both﴾ for that weaning.

When He, glorified is He, made clear that the period of nursing is two full years, He restricted it with His saying, ﴿for whoever wishes to complete the nursing﴾. Its apparent meaning is that if the father alone wishes to wean the child before the two years, that is permissible for him. Here, however, He, glorified is He, required the mutual consent and consultation of the two parents. Therefore the two matters must be combined, either by saying that the wish mentioned in "for whoever wishes to complete the nursing" must come from both of them, or by saying that this wish applies when the two parents are not both alive for the child, when only one of them is present, or when the nursing woman is a foster-mother for the child and not his mother.

Consultation (tashawur) is the extraction of an opinion. It is said: "I extracted honey (shurtu al-'asal)," meaning I took it out, and "I drove the animal (shurtu al-dabbah)," meaning I made it run to extract its running. So when one of the two parents wishes to wean the infant, he must gain the consent of the other and consult with him until agreement is reached between them on that.

His saying, ﴿And if you wish to seek a nurse for your children﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The implied meaning is that you seek nurses for your children other than the mother.

It is reported from Sibawayh that he omitted the lam, because the verb transitively takes two objects, and the first object is omitted, and the meaning is: that you seek nurses to nurse your children. ﴿There is no blame upon you if you hand over what you have given﴾, with a madd (to give), meaning what you have given. This is the reading of all except Ibn Kathir, who read it with qasr (to do), meaning what you have done. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

*And whatever good they obtained, they obtained it,*
*for it was inherited by the fathers of their fathers before.*

The meaning is that there is no harm upon you if you seek nurses for your children other than their mothers, when you hand over to the mothers their wage in accordance with what they have nursed for you up to the time of the decision to seek a nurse. This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri and Mujahid.

Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: the meaning of the verse is: when you hand over what you have given, namely the decision to seek a nurse. Each of the two parents hands it over and consents, and it is done by agreement between them, with good intention and with a desire for what is right. On this view, His saying "you have handed over" is general to men and women by way of predominance. On the first view, the address is to men alone.

It has also been said: the meaning is: when you hand over to whomever you intend to hire for nursing her wage. So the meaning is: when you hand over what you intend to give, that is, give it to the nursing women in accordance with what is customary, that is, in accordance with the wage of nursing women that people customarily know, without procrastination toward them or deducting part of what is due to them. For when their wage is not fully paid, it leads them to be lax about the child and to neglect his affairs.

Abd al-Razzaq, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan reported from Mujahid concerning His saying, ﴿The mothers shall nurse their children﴾: he said, "The divorced women, two years." He said, "two years." ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child﴾: he said, "She does not refuse to nurse him out of spite, in order to distress his father." ﴿Nor a father through his child﴾: he said, "The father is not to harm his child by preventing his mother from nursing him, in order to grieve her by that." ﴿And upon the heir﴾ [p. 159]: he said, "That is, the guardian, whoever is in that position." He said, "The maintenance in accordance with what is customary, its guardianship, and nursing him if the child has no property, and that his mother is not to be harmed." ﴿But if they both desire weaning by mutual consent and consultation﴾: he said, "They are not doing wrong to themselves or to their child." ﴿So there is no blame upon them both.﴾ ﴿And if you wish to seek a nurse for your children﴾: he said, "Fear of the child being lost." ﴿There is no blame upon you if you hand over what you have given in accordance with what is customary﴾: he said, "The reckoning of what the child was nursed with."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verse 233 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding the interpretation of this verse, that he said: What is meant by His words, ﴿And mothers shall breastfeed their children﴾, refers to the case of a man who divorces his wife while she has a child by him.

And regarding His words, ﴿when you pay what you give﴾, he said: it means what you give the wet-nurse (ẓi'r) beyond her wage (ajr).

Abu Dawud, in his Nasikh (the book on abrogating and abrogated texts), narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam regarding His words, ﴿And mothers shall breastfeed their children﴾, that he said: it refers to a woman who is divorced or whose husband dies leaving her.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning the woman who gives birth after six months, that she nurses for two full years, and if she gives birth after seven months, she nurses for twenty-three months. Then he recited: ﴿And his carrying and his weaning is thirty months﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 15].

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak regarding His words, ﴿And upon the one to whom the child belongs is their provision and their clothing according to what is customary﴾, that he said: according to one's means.

Abu Dawud, in his Nasikh, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam regarding His words, ﴿No mother shall be harmed through her child, nor a father through his child﴾, that: it is not permissible for her to throw her child upon him and he cannot find anyone to nurse him, nor is it permissible for him to harm her by taking the child from her while she wishes to nurse him. ﴿And upon the heir﴾, he said: it is the guardian of the deceased.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from 'Ata', Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi regarding His words, ﴿And upon the heir﴾, that he said: it is the heir of the infant, who spends upon him.

'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Qatadah something similar, and added: if the infant has no property, like what is owed by his father for the wage of nursing.

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated from al-Hasan something similar.

'Abd al-Razzaq and 'Abd ibn Humayd also narrated from Ibn Sirin something similar.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Qabisah ibn Dhu'ayb regarding His words, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾, that he said: it is the infant.

Waki' narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal something similar.

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾, that he said: he must not be harmed.

Ibn Jarir narrated from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿But if they both desire weaning﴾, that he said: it is weaning (al-fitam). 'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Mujahid, who said: consultation regarding what is less than two years; she may not wean him except with his consent, and he may not wean him except with her consent.

They also narrated from 'Ata' regarding His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And if you wish to seek a wet-nurse for your children﴾, that he said: [the wet-nurse is] his mother or another; ﴿then there is no blame upon you when you pay﴾, he said: when you pay her wage, ﴿what you give﴾.

When Glorified is He mentioned the waiting period (ʿiddah) for divorce and the mention of breastfeeding followed it, He then mentioned the waiting period for death, lest it be supposed that the waiting period for death is like the waiting period for divorce.

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is: "And those of you who die and leave wives," i.e., they have wives, so the wives shall wait (yatarabbaṣna).

Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: Its implied sense is: "And those of you who die and leave wives, their wives shall wait after them." It is like your saying: "Ghee is two manns for a dirham," i.e., "of it."

Al-Mahdawī related from Sībawayh that the meaning is: "And among what is recited to you is: those who die..." It has also been said that the implied sense is: "And the wives of those of you who die shall wait." This was mentioned by the author of al-Kashshāf. But it is objected that His saying ﴿and leave wives﴾ does not fit that implied sense, because the apparent meaning of a repeated indefinite noun is that it is different.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: The predicate concerning "those who..." is omitted, and the intended meaning is to inform about their wives, that they shall wait.

As for the wisdom in making the waiting period for death this amount: a male fetus usually begins to move at about three months, and a female at four months. So Allah, Glorified is He, added ten days to that, because the fetus may weaken in its movement, so its movement is delayed a little, but it is not delayed beyond this term.

The apparent meaning of this verse is general, and that every woman whose husband has died must observe this waiting period. But this generality has been specified by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their burden﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 4]. The majority of scholars held this view.

It is related from some of the Companions and a group of scholars that the pregnant woman observes the later of the two terms, combining the general and the specific and giving effect to both. But the truth is what the majority said.

Combining the general and the specific in this manner does not accord with the rules of the language or the principles of the Sharīʿah. There is no point in excluding the specific from among the members of the general except to show that its ruling differs from and contradicts the ruling of the general.

It is authentically reported from him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, that he (ﷺ) "permitted Subayʿah al-Aslamiyyah to marry after giving birth." The second waiting (tarabbuṣ) is the restraint from marriage.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that there is no distinction between the young and the old, the free and the slave, the one who menstruates and the one past childbearing, and that their waiting period in all cases for death is four months and ten days. It has been said that the waiting period of a slave woman is half that of a free woman: two months and five days.

Ibn al-ʿArabī said: "This is by consensus, except what is reported from al-Aṣamm, for he equated the free woman and the slave woman." Al-Bājī said: "We know of no disagreement on this except what is reported from Ibn Sīrīn, that he said: her waiting period is the waiting period of the free woman." But this is not firmly established from him. The basis of the view of al-Aṣamm and Ibn Sīrīn is the generality in this verse. The basis of the view of all others is analogy of the waiting period for death to the legal punishment (ḥadd), for it is halved for the slave woman by His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿Upon them is half the punishment of the chaste women﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 25].

The hadith has already been mentioned: "The divorce of a slave woman is two pronouncements, and her waiting period is two menstruations," and it is suitable to be used as evidence. What is meant by it is only to make her divorce half of a free woman's divorce and her waiting period half of the free woman's waiting period. But since it cannot be said that her divorce is one and a half pronouncements and her waiting period is one and a half menstruations, because that is not conceivable, her waiting period and her divorce were the amount mentioned in the hadith, as a making-up for the fraction. However, here there is a matter which prevents this analogy that the majority acted upon, namely that the wisdom in making the waiting period for death four months and ten days is what we mentioned earlier: knowing that the womb is free of pregnancy, which is known only through that period. There is no difference between the free woman and the slave woman in this matter, unlike the case of the waiting period not for death being two menstruations, for by that it is known that the womb is clear. The absence of distinction is confirmed by what will come concerning the waiting period of the umm walad.

The scholars differed concerning the waiting period of the umm walad (a slave woman who has borne her master's child) upon the death of her master.

Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Sīrīn, al-Zuhrī, ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, al-Awzāʿī, Isḥāq, Ibn Rāhawayh, and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal in one narration from him said: she observes four months and ten days, based on the hadith of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: "Do not confuse for us the sunnah of our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: The waiting period of the umm walad when her master dies is four months and ten days."

Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah and al-Ḥākim related it and al-Ḥākim declared it authentic, but Aḥmad and Abū ʿUbayd declared it weak.

Al-Dāraquṭnī said: "The correct report is that it is a statement of a Companion (mawqūf)."

Ṭāwūs and Qatādah said: her waiting period is two months and five nights.

Abū Ḥanīfah and his companions, al-Thawrī, and al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ said: she observes three menstrual cycles. This is the view of ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAṭāʾ and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī.

Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad in his well-known opinion said: her waiting period is one menstruation, and for the one who does not menstruate, one month. This is the view of Ibn ʿUmar, al-Shaʿbī, Makḥūl, al-Layth, Abū ʿUbayd, Abū Thawr and the majority.

His saying: ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾. Here "reaching" means the completion of the waiting period. ﴿there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves﴾ means adornment and making themselves available to suitors in a manner that is good, which does not contradict the Sharīʿah or customs that are considered praiseworthy.

This has been used as evidence for the obligation of mourning (iḥdād) upon the woman observing the waiting period for death.

It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others through more than one chain that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn over a dead person for more than three days, except over a husband, for four months and ten days." Likewise it is established from him, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others: "the prohibition of kohl for the one who is in the waiting period for death." Iḥdād is the abandoning of adornment, including perfume, wearing fine clothing, jewelry and other things. There is no disagreement on the obligation of this during the waiting period for death, and no disagreement that it is not obligatory during the revocable (rajʿiyyah) waiting period. They differed concerning the irrevocable (bāʾin) waiting period, on two opinions, and the place of this is the books of furūʿ (positive law).

Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan related from Ibn ʿAbbās concerning His saying: ﴿And those of you who die﴾: He said: "When a man died and left his wife, she would observe a waiting period of a year in his house, and he would provide for her from his property."

Then Allah revealed ﴿And those of you who die﴾ (the verse), and this became the waiting period for the woman whose husband has died, unless she is pregnant, in which case her waiting period is to give birth to what is in her womb.

He also said concerning her inheritance: ﴿And for them is one-fourth of what you leave﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 12], so He explained the inheritance of the woman and removed the bequest and maintenance. ﴿Then when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you﴾ means: when a woman is divorced or her husband dies, and when her waiting period has ended, there is no blame upon her if she adorns herself, beautifies herself, and makes herself available for marriage. That is the good (maʿrūf).

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Abū al-ʿĀliyah who said: "These ten days were added to the four months, because in the ten the soul is breathed into the fetus."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk concerning His saying: ﴿Then when they have reached their term﴾: he said: "When her waiting period has ended."

Ibn Abī Ḥātim related from Ibn Shihāb concerning His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾: he means her guardians.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Ḥākim related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he disliked perfume and adornment for the woman whose husband has died.

Mālik, ʿAbd al-Razzāq, the authors of the Sunan, and al-Tirmidhī and al-Ḥākim, who declared it authentic, related from al-Furayʿah bint Mālik ibn Sinān, who was the sister of Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, that she came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, asking to return to her family in Banū Khudrah, because her husband had gone out in pursuit of her slaves who had run away, until when he reached al-Qadūm (a place) they overtook him and killed him. She said: "I asked the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, to let me return to my family, for my husband did not leave me in a house he owned nor with maintenance." The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "Yes." So I departed, and when I was in the apartment (ḥujrah) or in the mosque, he called me or ordered that I be called, and I was called. He said: "How did you say it?"
