She said: "So I repeated to him the story I had mentioned to him about my husband." He said: "Remain in your house until the decree reaches its term."

She said: "So I observed the waiting period in it for four months and ten days." She said: "When ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān was caliph, he sent for me and asked me about that, and I informed him, so he followed it and ruled by it."

The commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on Surah 2, verses 235–236:

Al-junah (الجُناحُ) means sin (al-ithm), i.e., "there is no sin upon you." At-ta'rid (التَّعْرِيضُ, allusion) is the opposite of at-tasrih (التَّصْرِيحِ, explicit statement). It derives from ʿarada ash-shay', meaning he turned aside from it, as if circling around a thing without revealing it. It is also said that it derives from your saying ʿarradtu ar-rajul, meaning I gave the man a gift.

From this usage comes the report that "a group of Muslims gave the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr white garments," meaning they gifted them to both. Thus the one who speaks by allusion conveys to the other party speech whose meaning he understands.

In al-Kashshaf, it is said: The difference between al-kinayah (الكِنايَةِ, metonymy/indirect expression) and at-ta'rid is that al-kinayah is mentioning a thing by other than its proper word. At-ta'rid is mentioning something by which one indicates another thing that is not mentioned, as when the one in need says to the one whom he needs: "I came to you to greet you, and to look upon your noble face." For this reason they said:

"And it is enough for you, from me, of the greeting as a demand (for payment)."

It seems that it is inclining speech toward a side-meaning that points to the intended purpose, and it is called at-talwih (التَّلْوِيحُ, hinting) because what he intends shows through it (yalūḥu). End of quotation.

Al-khitbah (الخِطْبَةُ) with a kasrah (kasr) is what the seeker does by way of requesting and courting with speech and action. It is said: khatabahā, yakhtubuhā, khitbatan and khitban.

As for al-khutbah (الخُطْبَةُ) with a dammah on the kha', it is the speech that a man delivers while proposing.

His saying "akinntum" (أكْنَنْتُمْ) means you concealed and kept hidden, of marriage after the end of the waiting period.

Al-iknan (الإكْنانُ) is concealment and hiding. It is said: akantuhu and kanantuhu with one meaning.

From this comes "bayḍun maknūn" (hidden eggs) and "durrun maknūn" (hidden pearl).

Also from it: akanna al-bayt sahibahu, meaning the house sheltered its occupant (i.e., covered him).

His saying ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾ means: Allah knows that you cannot refrain from speaking to them, because of your desire for them. So He permitted you allusion but not explicit statement.

In al-Kashshaf: In it there is a touch of reproach, like His saying: ﴿Allah knows that you were betraying yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187].

His saying ﴿but do not promise them in secret﴾ means: "in secret" (ʿala sirr), so the preposition was omitted, because the verb does not transitively take two objects.

The scholars have differed about the meaning of as-sirr (السِّرِّ, secret). It has been said: its meaning is marriage (nikāḥan), i.e., a man should not say to this woman in her waiting period, "Marry me," but should instead allude indirectly. The majority of scholars have taken this as the meaning of the verse.

It has been said: as-sirr is fornication (az-zina), i.e., there should not be among you a promise regarding fornication during the waiting period and then marriage after it. This was said by Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Mijlaz, al-Hasan, Qatadah, ad-Dahhak, and an-Nakhaʿi, and at-Tabari (aṭ-Ṭabarī) chose it.

From this is the saying of al-Hutay'ah:

"The secret of their neighbour is forbidden to them, / while their neighbour eats the noses of the dishes."

It has been said: as-sirr is intercourse, i.e., do not describe yourselves to them with frequent intercourse to make them desire marriage. This is the view taken by ash-Shafiʿi regarding the meaning of the verse. From this is also the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"Has Basbasah claimed today that I / have grown old, and that such as I do not do well at the secret?"

Similar to it is the saying of al-Aʿsha:

"So you will not seek her secret for her wealth, / nor will you give her up for her poverty."

He meant: you seek her marriage for the abundance of her wealth, and you will not let her go for the scarcity of her wealth. The use of the "but" (lākin) in His saying ﴿but﴾ is a resumption (istidrak) from a deleted assumed element indicated by ﴿you will remember them﴾, i.e., "so remember them, ﴿but do not promise them in secret﴾."

Ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: The community has agreed that speaking to a woman in her waiting period with anything that is obscene (rafath), such as mention of intercourse or urging toward it, is not permitted.

He also said: The community has agreed on the disapproval (karāhah) of making a promise during the waiting period to the woman herself, to the father regarding his virgin daughter, and to the master regarding his female slave.

His saying ﴿except that you say a fair word﴾: It has been said that this is an exceptive (istithnāʾ) that is disjunctive (munqaṭiʿ) with the meaning of "but" (lākin), and the fair word is what is permitted of allusion.

The author of al-Kashshaf rejected that it is disjunctive and said: It is an exception from His saying ﴿do not promise them﴾, i.e., do not promise them any promise at all except a known promise, not a reprehensible one. On this basis he made it an exception of the type called mufarragh (مُفَرَّغًا, exception with the excluded element omitted). The reason for rejecting that it is disjunctive is that it would lead to making allusion a thing promised, and this is not so, because allusion is a means of promising, not the thing promised itself.

His saying ﴿and do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾: The discussion of the meaning of al-ʿazm (العَزْمِ, resolve) has already preceded. It is said: ʿazama ash-shay' and ʿazama ʿalayhi. The meaning here is: do not resolve upon concluding the marriage contract, then ʿalā was deleted.

Sibawayh said: Deletion in this verse is not to be used as a basis for analogy (lā yuqāsu ʿalayhi).

An-Nahhas said: It is possible that the meaning is "do not conclude the tie of marriage," because the meaning of "resolve" (taʿzimū) and "conclude" (taʿqidū) is one. It has been said: resolving upon an action precedes it, so in this prohibition there is an emphasis, because when one is prohibited from what precedes a thing, the prohibition of that thing is all the more so.

His saying ﴿until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾ means: until the waiting period is completed. Al-kitāb (الكِتابُ, the prescribed writ) here is the limit and the measure of the term that was determined. He called it "book" because it is limited and obligatory, like His saying the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been enjoined upon the believers as a decreed obligation﴾ [an-Nisāʾ: 103]. This ruling, namely the prohibition of concluding a marriage contract during the waiting period, is agreed upon (muʿjamaʿun ʿalayhi).

ʿAbd ar-Razzaq, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, al-Bukhari, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi have related from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿There is no sin upon you regarding what you allude to of the proposal to women﴾, that he said: Allusion is that you say: "I intend to marry, and I truly love a woman for her affairs and her matters, and it is my nature to be with women, and I would wish that Allah would make easy for me a righteous woman."

Ibn Jarir related from him that he says to her: "If you see that you do not outpace me with yourself, and I would wish that Allah had arranged between me and you," and similar to this speech.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him that he said: He says: "I am truly desirous of you, and I would wish that I had married you."

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿or you conceal [it] in yourselves﴾ that he said: "You kept it secret."

ʿAbd ar-Razzaq related the same from ad-Dahhak.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir related from al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿Allah knows that you will remember them﴾ that he said: "With the sin."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir related from Mujahid that he said: "His mentioning her within himself."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying ﴿but do not promise them in secret﴾ that he said: He says to her: "I am a lover, and make a pledge to me that you will not marry anyone other than me," and similar to this. ﴿except that you say a fair word﴾, which is his saying: "If you see that you do not outpace me with yourself."

Ibn Jarir related from him regarding the "secret" that it is fornication: a man would come in order to commit fornication while alluding to marriage.

ʿAbd ar-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir related from him regarding His saying ﴿except that you say a fair word﴾ that he said: "He says: 'Indeed you are beautiful, and indeed you are good for me, and indeed women are part of my need.'"

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim related from him regarding His saying ﴿and do not resolve upon the tie of marriage﴾ that he said: "Do not marry," ﴿until the prescribed term reaches its end﴾ he said: "until the waiting period is completed."

The meaning of "no blame" (junah) here is responsibility for the dower (mahr) and the like. So its removal means: there is no responsibility upon you for the dower or the like if you divorce the women in the described condition. The "mā" in His words ﴿as long as you have not touched them﴾ is a verbal (temporal) masdar-type particle, with an omitted noun: "the period of your not touching them."

Abu al-Baqa' reported that it is a conditional particle, in the construction of a condition being attached to a condition (i'tiraḍ al-shart 'ala al-shart), so that the second condition qualifies the first, as in your saying: "If you come to me, if you treat me well, I will honour you," meaning: "If you come to me doing good to me." The meaning would then be: "If you divorce them while not having touched them."

It has also been said that it is a relative pronoun: "If you divorce the women whom you have not touched." The scholars likewise differed concerning His words ﴿or you have decreed for them an obligation﴾. It was said that "aw" means "illa" (except): "except that you decree." It was said that it means "hatta" (until): "until you decree." It was said that it means "wa" (and): "and you decree."

I do not see any value in this lengthy discussion. The meaning of the verse is too clear to be confused. God, glorified is He, lifted the blame from those who divorce as long as neither of the two circumstances has occurred, that is, for the period in which that one of the two is absent. An indefinite "one of the two" is not negated except by the negation of both together. If touching occurs, the stated dower (musamma) or the equivalent dower (mahr al-mithl) becomes obligatory. If the decree of an obligation occurs, half of it becomes obligatory in the absence of touching. Each of these is a "junah" (i.e., the stated dower, or half of it, or the equivalent dower).

Know that the divorced women are of four kinds:

1. A woman who has been touched and for whom an obligation was decreed. This is the one mentioned earlier before this verse, and in it there is a prohibition for husbands from taking back anything of what they have given them, and that their waiting period ('idda) is three menstrual cycles (qurū').

2. A woman for whom no obligation was decreed and who has not been touched. This is the one mentioned here, so she has no dower, but only a provision (mut'a). In Surat al-Aḥzāb it is clarified that when a woman who has not been touched is divorced, she has no waiting period.

3. A woman for whom an obligation was decreed but who has not been touched. This is the one referred to by His words, glorified is He, here: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you had decreed for them an obligation﴾. 

4. A woman who has been touched but for whom no obligation was decreed. This is the one mentioned in His words, exalted is He: ﴿So whatever you have enjoyed of them, give them their wages﴾ [an-Nisa': 24]. By His words ﴿as long as you have not touched them﴾ is meant "as long as you have not had intercourse with them." Ibn Mas'ud recited: "min qabli an tujāmi'ūhunna" (before you have intercourse with them). Ibn Jarir transmitted this from him.

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim recited ﴿mā lam tamassūhunna﴾. Ḥamza and al-Kisa'i recited "tamāsūhunna" from the form of mufā'ala (reciprocal form). The "farīḍa" here means the naming of the dower.

His words: "And provide for them" mean: give them something that serves as provision for them. The apparent sense of the command is obligation, and this was the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Umar, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilaba, al-Zuhri, Qatada and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Among the proofs of obligation is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period which you could count for them; so provide for them and release them with a fair release﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 49].

Mālik, Abu 'Ubayd, the judge Shurayḥ and others said: the provision (mut'a) for the woman mentioned here is recommended (mandūb), not obligatory, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a duty upon the doers of good﴾. Had it been obligatory, He would have made it binding upon all creation. This is answered by saying that this does not contradict obligation; rather it is an emphasis upon it, as in His saying in another verse: ﴿a duty upon the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqara: 241], meaning that fulfilling this and carrying it out is the matter of the people of piety, and every Muslim is obliged to fear God, glorified is He.

There has also been disagreement over whether the provision is prescribed for women other than this divorcee, who was divorced before touching and before the decreeing of an obligation, or whether it is prescribed only for her. It was said: it is prescribed for every divorced woman. This was the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, 'Ata', Jabir ibn Zayd, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliya, al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions, Aḥmad and Isḥāq. But they differed as to whether it is obligatory for women other than the one divorced before consummation and before the decreeing of an obligation, or recommended only. They cited His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for divorced women is a provision according to what is customary, a duty upon the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqara: 241], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives: if you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a fair release﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 28]. The first verse is general for every divorced woman, and the second concerns the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), who had been given obligations and had been consummated with.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: it is obligatory for the divorced woman when she is divorced before touching, even if an obligation had been decreed for her, because of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period which you could count for them; so provide for them﴾ [al-Aḥzāb: 49]. He said: this verse in al-Aḥzāb abrogated the one in al-Baqara.

A group of scholars held that the provision is specific to the woman divorced before consummation and before naming a dower, because the one who has been consummated is entitled to the full stated dower or the equivalent dower, while the unconsummated woman for whom her husband decreed an obligation, that is, named a dower for her and divorced her before consummation, is entitled to half the stated dower. Among those who held this were Ibn 'Umar and Mujahid.

There is consensus that a woman divorced before consummation and before an obligation was decreed is entitled only to the provision, if she is free.

As for a slave woman, the majority held that she has the provision. al-Awza'i and al-Thawri said: she has no provision, because she belongs to her master, and he is not entitled to wealth in exchange for distressing his property; because God, glorified is He, prescribed the provision for the divorced woman before consummation and decreeing, on account of her being distressed by divorce before that.

They differed about whether the prescribed provision is fixed by a measure or not. Mālik and al-Shafi'i in his new opinion said: there is no known limit for it, but rather whatever falls under the name "provision."

Abu Ḥanifa said: if the spouses dispute the amount of the provision, she is owed half the equivalent dower (mahr mithlihā), and it may not fall below five dirhams, because the least dower is ten dirhams.

The early generation (salaf) had opinions about it that will be mentioned, God willing.

His words: ﴿According to the wealthy his measure, and according to the straitened his measure﴾ indicate that the consideration in this is the condition of the husband, so the provision from the rich is greater than the provision from the poor.

The majority recited ﴿ʿalā al-mūsiʿ﴾ with a sukūn on the waw and a kasra on the sin, meaning one whose circumstances have become ample.

Abu Ḥaywa recited it with a fatḥa on the waw and a tashdīd and fatḥa on the sin.

Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr recited "qadruhu" with a sukūn on the dāl in both places. Ibn 'Amir, Ḥamza, al-Kisa'i and 'Asim in the narration of Ḥafs recited with a fatḥa on the dāl in both places.

al-Akhfash and others said: both are eloquent dialects. The same is recited in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so the valleys flowed with their measure﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17], and His saying: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾ [al-An'am: 91].

"Al-muqtir" is the one of limited means. "Matā'an" is a masdar emphasising "wa mattiʿūhunna" (and provide for them). "Al-ma'rūf" is what is known in the law and in custom that agrees with it.

His words: "ḥaqqan" is either an attribute of "matā'an," or a masdar for an omitted verb, meaning: that is a duty, a duty. It is said: "ḥaqqaqtu 'alayhi al-qaḍā'" and "aḥqaqtu," meaning: I made it obligatory upon him.

His words: ﴿And if you divorce them before you have touched them﴾ to the end of the verse. In it is evidence that the provision is not obligatory for this divorcee, because it stands in contrast to the divorcee before consummation and decreeing who is entitled to the provision.

His words: ﴿then half of what you have decreed﴾ mean: what is obligatory upon you is half of what you named for them of the dower. This is agreed upon.

The majority recited "fa-niṣfu" in the nominative (raf'). Others than the majority recited it in the accusative (naṣb), meaning: then pay half of what you have decreed. It was also recited with a ḍamma and a kasra on the nūn, and both are dialects.

There is also agreement that a woman whose husband did not consummate with her and who died after he had decreed a dower for her is entitled to the full dower by death, and she inherits, and she observes the waiting period.

They differed concerning seclusion (khalwa): whether it takes the place of consummation, so that the woman is entitled to the full dower by it as she is entitled to it by consummation, or not. Mālik, al-Shafi'i in his older opinion, the Kufans, the Rightly-Guided Caliphs and the majority of scholars held the first view, and according to them the waiting period is also obligatory.

al-Shafi'i in his new opinion said: only half the dower is obligatory, and this is the apparent sense of the verse, because touching (mass) was explained to mean intercourse; and according to him the waiting period is not obligatory. This was the view of a group of the early generation.

His words: ﴿unless they pardon﴾ refer to the divorcees, and its meaning: they leave it and forgive. Its form is "yaf'alna." It is an exception that is "mufarragh" (lacking a stated object) from the most general of the general; and it was said it is "munqaṭi'" (disjunctive), and its meaning: they leave the half that is due to them from the husbands.

The nūn did not drop with "in" because the plural feminine in the imperfect has one form in the nominative, accusative and jussive, the nūn being a pronoun and not a sign of i'rab, as in the masculine in your saying: "al-rijālu ya'fūna" (the men pardon). This is the view of the majority of exegetes.

It is related from Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi that he said: "illā an ya'fūna" refers to the men, but this is weak in wording.

The meaning of His words: ﴿or the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage pardons﴾ is conjoined (ma'ṭūf) upon the grammatical position (maḥall) of "illā an ya'fūna," because the first is indeclinable (mabnī) and this is declinable (mu'rab). It was said: he is the husband, and this was the view of Jubayr ibn Muṭ'im, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Shurayḥ, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, al-Sha'bi, 'Ikrima, Nafi', Ibn Sirin, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Muḥammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Jabir ibn Zayd, Abu Mijlaz, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Iyas ibn Mu'awiya, Makhul, Muqatil ibn Ḥayyan, and it is the new opinion of al-Shafi'i. This was also the view of Abu Ḥanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, Ibn Shubruma and al-Awza'i, and Ibn Jarir preferred it.

In this view there is both strength and weakness. Its strength is that the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage in reality is the husband, because it is he to whom its lifting is by divorce. Its weakness is that pardon from him is not intelligible, and what they said, that his pardon means he gives her the full dower, is not apparent, because pardon is not applied to an increase.

It was said: the meaning of His words ﴿or the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage﴾ is the guardian (walī), and this was the view of al-Nakha'i, 'Alqama, al-Ḥasan, Ṭawus, 'Ata', Abu al-Zinad, Zayd ibn Aslam, Rabi'a, al-Zuhri, al-Aswad ibn Yazid, al-Sha'bi, Qatada, Mālik, and al-Shafi'i in his older opinion. In it there is strength and weakness. Its strength is that the meaning of pardon in it is intelligible. Its weakness is that the knot of marriage is in the hand of the husband, not in his hand. What further weakens this view is that the guardian has no right to pardon the husband from what he does not own.

al-Qurtubi related a consensus that the guardian owns nothing of her property, and the dower is her property.

So the preponderant view is that of the earlier scholars, for two reasons. First: the husband is the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage in reality. Second: his pardon by completing the dower proceeds from one with full right of disposal, unlike the guardian. Calling the increase "pardon," though contrary to the apparent sense, is intelligible because the common practice was for them to hand over the full dower at the contract, so pardon was understood: he left it to her and did not reclaim half of it. There is no need to say that it is by way of mushākala (a rhetorical figure of association, using one word because of another related to it), as in al-Kashshāf, because it is genuine pardon, i.e., leaving what is entitled to be claimed, unless it is said that it is mushākala, or that it is good for him to complete the dower before the husband sends it.

His words: ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to piety﴾. It was said: it is an address to men and women by way of predominance (taghlīb). The majority recited it with the feminine second-person ta' (tā'), while Abu Nahīk and al-Sha'bi recited it with the yā' (yā'), in which case the address is to men.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verse 237 (part 2 of 2):

This is evidence for what we have preferred, that the one who holds the "knot of marriage" (ʿuqdat al-nikāḥ) is the husband, because a guardian's pardoning of something he does not own is not closer to piety; rather, it is closer to injustice and oppression.

His saying: ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you﴾ was recited by the majority with a ḍamma on the waw. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar recited it with a kasra, and ʿAlī, Mujāhid, Abū Ḥaywa and Ibn Abī ʿAbla recited "wa-lā tanāsawū" (تَناسَوُا). The meaning is that the spouses should not forget the favour each of them shows to the other. Among that is that the woman show graciousness by pardoning half, and the man show graciousness to her by completing the dowry. This is a guidance to men and women among spouses to abandon scrutinizing one another and to be lenient regarding what one of them takes from the other, on account of the bond that has come about through the mutual reaching of each other, a bond to which no other bond is comparable. So, from observing its right and knowing it as it should be known, is the eagerness of both of them for leniency.

His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ contains, in encouraging the doer of good and warning against others, what is not hidden.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding his saying: ﴿as long as you have not touched them or specified for them an obligatory dowry﴾, that he said: "The touching is intercourse (al-nikāḥ), and the obligation is the dowry. ﴿Provide for them﴾: it is upon the man who marries a woman and has not specified a dowry for her, then divorces her before he has entered upon her. Allah commanded him to provide for her according to his capacity and his means. If he is wealthy, he provides her with a servant; if he is poor, he provides her with three garments or something like that."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Ḥātim transmitted from him that he said: "The provision of divorce: the highest of it is a servant, and below that is silver, and below that is clothing."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: "The least that the provision may be is thirty dirhams."

al-Qurṭubī in his tafsir narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī that he provided with twenty thousand and a quantity of honey.

And from Shurayḥ that he provided with five hundred dirhams.

al-Dāraquṭnī transmitted from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī that he provided with ten thousand.

ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted from Ibn Sīrīn that he used to provide with a servant and maintenance, or with clothing.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim and al-Bayhaqī in his Sunan transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding his saying: ﴿before you touch them﴾ that he said: "The touching is intercourse. So she has half of her dowry, and she has no more than that, unless they pardon." (p-164) This refers to the previously married woman (al-thayyib) and the virgin (al-bikr) whom someone other than her father marries off. Allah made the pardon theirs: if they wish, they pardon by leaving it, and if they wish, they take half the dowry. ﴿Or the one in whose hand is the knot of marriage pardons﴾: this is the father of the virgin girl. The pardon is given to him; she has no say with him when she is divorced, as long as she is in his guardianship.

al-Shāfiʿī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said concerning a man who marries a woman, then is alone with her but does not touch her, then divorces her: "She has nothing but half the dowry, because Allah says: ﴿And if you divorce them﴾," the verse.

al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: "She has half the dowry, even if he sat between her legs."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim, al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ and al-Bayhaqī with a good chain transmitted from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The one in whose hand is the knot of marriage is the husband."

Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn Abi Ḥātim, al-Dāraquṭnī and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from ʿAlī the like of it, as his own saying.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās the like of it.

Ibn Abi Ḥātim and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from him that he said: "It is her father, her brother, and whoever she may not be married except with his permission."

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn Jarir transmitted from Mujāhid regarding his saying: ﴿And do not forget graciousness between you﴾ that he said: "In this or otherwise."

ʿAbd al-Razzāq, Ibn Abi Shayba, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, al-Tirmidhī, who authenticated it, al-Nasāʾī, Ibn Māja, al-Ḥākim, who authenticated it, and al-Bayhaqī transmitted that: "A people came to Ibn Masʿūd and said: 'A man among us married a woman, did not specify a dowry for her, did not consummate with her, until he died.' He said: 'I see that I should give her a dowry like the dowry of her women, neither deficient nor excessive, and she has the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period of four months and ten days.' Some people of Ashja', among them Maghqal ibn Sinān, heard of that and said: 'We testify that you have decided the same as what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) decided concerning a woman among us called Barwaʿ bint Wāshiq.'"

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from ʿAlī that he said concerning a woman whose husband died without his having specified a dowry for her: "She has the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period, and she has no dowry."

And he said: "The saying of a bedouin from Ashja' is not accepted against the Book of Allah."

al-Shāfiʿī and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said concerning a woman whose husband dies and he had specified a dowry for her: "She has the dowry and the inheritance."

Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb that he decided concerning a woman whom a man marries: that when the curtains are let down, the dowry becomes due.

Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from ʿUmar and ʿAlī that he said: "If he lets down a curtain and closes a door, she has the full dowry, and upon her is the waiting period."

Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, Ibn Abi Shayba and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Zurāra ibn Awfā that he said: "The rightly-guided caliphs decided that whoever closes a door or lets down a curtain, the dowry and the waiting period become due."

Mālik and al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Zayd ibn Thābit something similar.

al-Bayhaqī transmitted from Muḥammad ibn Thawbān that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever uncovers a woman and looks at her private part, the dowry becomes due."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 2):

Al-muhafaẓa ʿala al-shay' (guarding/maintaining something) means persisting in it and being constant in it. Al-Wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ, and the awsaṭ (or wasaṭ) of a thing is its best part.

From this is the saying of Allah, ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. From it is also the saying of some of the Arabs praising the Prophet (ﷺ):

"O best of people in all their glories, and most noble of people in mother and father, both righteous."

And "Fulan wasaṭa al-qawm yasiṭuhum" means he came to be in the middle of the people. Allah singled out al-Ṣalāh al-Wusṭā (the middle prayer) for mention after its inclusion in the generality of the prayers, honouring it.

Abu Jaʿfar read "wa-al-ṣalāta al-wusṭā" with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (al-ighrāʾ, i.e., a call to attention), and likewise al-Ḥulwānī read it. Qalūn, on the authority of Nafiʿ, read "al-wuṣṭā" with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭāʾ; the two are dialectal variants, like al-sirāṭ and al-ṣirāṭ.

The scholars have differed in determining it into eighteen opinions, which I have set out in my commentary on al-Muntaqā, and I mentioned what each group relied upon. The most preferred and soundest of the opinions is that of the majority, that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, because of what is established in al-Bukhari, Muslim, the authors of the Sunan, and others, from the hadith of ʿAli, who said: "We used to think it was the Fajr prayer until I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the day of the Confederates: 'They have kept us busy from the middle prayer, the ʿAṣr prayer. May Allah fill their graves and their bellies with fire.'"

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others also related a similar hadith from Ibn Masʿud, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani also related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Bazzar related it with a sound chain from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Bazzar also related it with a sound chain from Ḥudhayfa, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Tabarani related it with a weak chain from Umm Salama, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

There are hadiths traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer without mention of the day of the Confederates: among them from Ibn ʿUmar in Ibn Mandah; among them from Samura in Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani; among them also from him in Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi authenticated it; and from Abu Hurayra in Ibn Jarir, al-Bayhaqi and al-Tahawi.

It was also related from him by Ibn Saʿid, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani; from Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Bazzar with sound chains; and from Abu Malik al-Ashʿari in Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani. These are hadiths traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer.

Great reports from the Companions also exist stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, and in what is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) there is what makes further evidence unnecessary.

As for what is related from ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas that they said: it is the Ṣubḥ prayer, as Malik related in the Muwatta' from them both; Ibn Jarir related it from Ibn ʿAbbas; likewise ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related it from him; likewise Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Ibn ʿUmar; likewise Ibn Jarir related it from Jabir; likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Abu Umama. All of these are from their own statements, and there is nothing among them traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Such reports do not constitute proof, especially when they oppose what is established from him (ﷺ) with an establishment that can be claimed to be mass-transmitted (mutawatir). If the reports of the Companions do not constitute proof, then the reports of those after them, the Successors and their followers, are even less so.

Likewise, what Ibn Abi Hatim related with a good chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: the middle prayer is Maghrib, does not constitute proof. Likewise no weight is given to what came from a group of Companions that it is Zuhr or other prayers. Rather, what one who needs careful reflection should consider is what came traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) indicating that it is Zuhr, as Ibn Jarir related from Zayd ibn Thabit, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The middle prayer is the Ẓuhr prayer."

But its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is not sound; rather, what is related from Zayd ibn Thabit is his own statement. Evidence for this was drawn from the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at al-hājira (midday), and it was the heaviest prayer for his Companions. But where does this argument stand against those sound, established hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ)? Likewise, no weight is given to what is related from Ibn ʿUmar as his own statement that it is Zuhr.

The same applies to what is related from ʿAʾisha, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and others. There is no proof in the statement of anyone against the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

As for what ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and others related, that Ḥafṣa said to her freedman Abu Rafiʿ, when she had ordered him to write a Qur'an codex for her: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, come to me so I may dictate it to you." When he reached it, she ordered him to write: "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer."

Malik, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan also related it from her, and they added: she said, "I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Malik, Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others related from Abu Yunus, the freedman of ʿAʾisha, that she ordered him to write a codex for her and said: "When you reach this verse, inform me: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." He said: "When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer.'" ʿAʾisha said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Waki', Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Umm Salama that she ordered someone to write a codex for her and told him what Ḥafṣa and ʿAʾisha had said.

The utmost that these reports from the three Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, establish is that they transmitted this wording in this way from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There is nothing in them indicating that the middle prayer is Zuhr or otherwise. Rather, the most that the conjoining of the ʿAṣr prayer to the middle prayer indicates is that it is other than it, because the conjoined is other than that to which it is conjoined. This argument does not conflict with what is established from him (ﷺ) with an establishment that does not preclude that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, as we have already explained.

The conclusion: this reading transmitted by the three Mothers of the Believers, with the inclusion of "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr," is opposed by what Ibn Jarir related from ʿUrwa, who said: "In the codex of ʿAʾisha it was: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the ʿAṣr prayer.'"

Waki' related from Ḥumayda, who said: "I read in the codex of ʿAʾisha: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr.'"

Ibn Abi Dawud related the same from Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abu ʿUbayd related from Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam that ʿAʾisha ordered that her codex be written and said: "When you reach ﴿Guard the prayers﴾, do not write it until you inform me." When they informed her that they had reached it, she said: "Write it: the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr."

Ibn Jarir, al-Tahawi and al-Bayhaqi related from ʿAmr ibn Rafiʿ, who said: "It was written in the codex of Ḥafṣa: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the prayer of ʿAṣr.'"

Abu ʿUbayd in his Fada'il and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he used to recite it: "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr."

Abu ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Jarir and al-Tahawi related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite it: "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr."

Al-Mahamili related from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid that he recited it likewise. These reports oppose those reports with respect to recitation and transmission of the reading, and what is sound from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding the determination remains clear of the turbidity of opposition.

Moreover, there is what indicates the abrogation (naskh) of that reading which Ḥafṣa, ʿAʾisha and Umm Salama transmitted.

ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi related from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: "There was revealed: 'Guard the prayers and the prayer of ʿAṣr,' and we recited it during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for as long as Allah willed. Then Allah abrogated it, and revealed: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." It was said to him: "So it is the ʿAṣr prayer?" He said: "I have told you how it was revealed and how Allah abrogated it. And Allah knows best."

Al-Bayhaqi related the same from him by another route.

When this has been established for you, and you know what we have cited, it becomes clear that nothing has come that opposes the view that the middle prayer is the ʿAṣr prayer. As for the proofs of the remaining opinions, there is nothing among them worth occupying oneself with, because nothing has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) on the matter. Some of those who said it is a particular prayer relied on a matter not to be relied upon, saying: it is such-and-such a prayer because it is the middle one relative to the number of prayers before it and after it. This is mere opinion and pure conjecture, which Shariʿa rulings should not rest upon even if there were nothing opposing it from the Prophet (ﷺ), so how much more so when there is what is at the highest level of soundness, strength and establishment from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)? How astonishing it is, by Allah, regarding a people who were not content with their shortcoming in the knowledge of the Sunna and their turning away from the best and most beneficial sciences, until they burdened themselves with speaking about the rulings of Allah and presuming to interpret the Book of Allah without knowledge or guidance, so they came with what is laughable at times and weeping-worthy at others.

His saying: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion (qanitin)﴾. Qunut was said to mean obedience, i.e., stand before Allah in your prayer obediently. This was said by Jabir ibn Zayd, ʿAṭāʾ, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Shaʿbi. It was also said to mean humility (khushuʿ), said by Ibn ʿUmar and Mujahid.

From it is the saying of the poet:

"Devoted to Allah, calling upon his Lord, and withdrawing from the people deliberately."

It was also said to mean supplication, and Ibn ʿAbbas said this.

In a hadith: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed qunut for a month, supplicating against Ri'l and Dhakwan."

Some said qunut means prolonging the standing. It was also said its meaning is silence, said by al-Suddi, and the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and others supports this, where he said: "A man used to speak with his companion during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) about a need during the prayer, until this verse was revealed: ﴿And stand before Allah in devotion﴾, so we were commanded to be silent." It was also said that the root meaning of qunut in the language is persistence in a thing, so any meaning that suits persistence may validly be attributed to qunut.

The scholars have mentioned that qunut has thirteen meanings, which we have mentioned in our commentary on al-Muntaqā. The one that is determinate here is to interpret qunut as silence, due to the hadith mentioned.

His saying: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. Fear (khawf) is alarm. Rijal is the plural of rajul or rajil, from the saying "rajila al-insan yarjalu rajilan," when a person lacks a mount and walks on his feet; so he is a rajul and rajil.

The people of the Ḥijāz say: "So-and-so walked barefoot to the House of Allah, rajulan."

This was related by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari and others.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 2 of 2):

When Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the command to be vigilant in observing the prayers, He mentioned the state of fear, that in it they neglect what is within their capacity and what falls within their power of observing the prayer by performing it while on foot and while riding, and He made clear to them that this worship is obligatory in all circumstances according to what is possible.

The scholars have differed over the limit of fear that permits this, and the discussion is thoroughly treated in the books of furu' (positive law).

His saying: ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ﴾ (So when you are secure) means: when your fear has passed, return to what you were commanded of completing the prayer, facing the qiblah, observing all its conditions and pillars. This is His saying: ﴿فاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَما عَلَّمَكُمْ﴾ (then remember Allah as He taught you). It has been said that the meaning of the verse is: "when you have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence," but this is contrary to the meaning of the verse.

His saying: ﴿كَما عَلَّمَكُمْ﴾ (as He taught you) means: like what He taught you of the laws, ﴿ما لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ (what you did not used to know). The kaf (as) is an adjective of a deleted verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning: a remembrance existing like His teaching you, or like His teaching you.

Ibn Jarir reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ differed concerning the middle prayer, like this, and he interlaced his fingers.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Umar that he was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: "It is among them, so guard them all."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Zayd ibn Thabit that a man asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: "Be vigilant over the prayers and you will attain it."

Ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Abd ibn Humayd reported from al-Rabi' ibn Khaytham that a questioner asked him about the middle prayer, and he said: "Be vigilant over them, for if you do, you will hit it; it is only one of them."

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported from Ibn Sirin, who said: Shurayh was asked about the middle prayer, and he said: "Be vigilant over it and you will hit it."

We have already mentioned what has been related from the Prophet ﷺ and from his companions, may Allah be pleased with them, concerning its specification.

al-Tabarani reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿وقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾ (and stand before Allah in devout obedience), a statement like what we have already mentioned from Zayd ibn Arqam.

Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Mas'ud something similar.

Sa'id ibn Mansur and 'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Muhammad ibn Ka'b something similar as well.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from 'Ikrimah something similar.

'Abd al-Razzaq, 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir reported from Mujahid something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿وقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾, he said: "Praying."

Ibn Jarir reported from him concerning the verse, he said: "Every people of a religion stand in it disobedient; stand you in obedience."

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported from al-Dahhak something like it.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir reported from Mujahid concerning His saying: ﴿وقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قانِتِينَ﴾, he said: "From qunut (devout obedience) is ruku' (bowing) and khushu' (humility), and the length of ruku' meaning the length of standing, lowering the gaze, lowering the wing, and awe before Allah."

It is established in the two Sahihs and other works from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed, in the prayer there is preoccupation." And in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, this prayer is not fit for anything of the speech of people; it is only glorification, magnification and recitation of the Qur'an."

The traditions have differed concerning the qunut that is agreed upon: whether it is before ruku' or after it, whether it is in all prayers or some of them, and whether it is specific to calamities (nawazil) or not. The preferred view is that it is specific to calamities.

We have explained this in our commentary on al-Muntaqa, so let him refer to it.

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجالًا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾ (So if you fear, then on foot or riding), he said: "The rider prays on his mount, and the one on foot on his feet," ﴿فاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَما عَلَّمَكم ما لَمْ تَكُونُوا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ meaning: as He taught you to pray, the rider on his mount and the one on foot on his feet.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When there is close fighting, let him gesture with his head wherever his face is; this is His saying: ﴿فَرِجالًا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said concerning ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجالًا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾: "One rak'ah at a time."

Waki' and Ibn Jarir reported from Mujahid concerning ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ﴾, he said: "You have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 2, verses 238–239 (part 1 of 2):

Al-muhafaẓa ʿala al-shay' (guarding/maintaining something) means persisting in it and being constant in it. Al-Wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ, and the awsaṭ (or wasaṭ) of a thing is its best part.

From this is the saying of Allah, ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. From it is also the saying of some of the Arabs praising the Prophet (ﷺ):

"O best of people in all their glories, and most noble of people in mother and father, both righteous."

And "Fulan wasaṭa al-qawm yasiṭuhum" means he came to be in the middle of the people. Allah singled out al-Ṣalāh al-Wusṭā (the middle prayer) for mention after its inclusion in the generality of the prayers, honouring it.

Abu Jaʿfar read "wa-al-ṣalāta al-wusṭā" with the accusative (naṣb) as an incitement (al-ighrāʾ, i.e., a call to attention), and likewise al-Ḥulwānī read it. Qalūn, on the authority of Nafiʿ, read "al-wuṣṭā" with the ṣād, due to the proximity of the ṭāʾ; the two are dialectal variants, like al-sirāṭ and al-ṣirāṭ.

The scholars have differed in determining it into eighteen opinions, which I have set out in my commentary on al-Muntaqā, and I mentioned what each group relied upon. The most preferred and soundest of the opinions is that of the majority, that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, because of what is established in al-Bukhari, Muslim, the authors of the Sunan, and others, from the hadith of ʿAli, who said: "We used to think it was the Fajr prayer until I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say on the day of the Confederates: 'They have kept us busy from the middle prayer, the ʿAṣr prayer. May Allah fill their graves and their bellies with fire.'"

Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and others also related a similar hadith from Ibn Masʿud, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani also related it from Ibn ʿAbbas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Bazzar related it with a sound chain from Jabir, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Bazzar also related it with a sound chain from Ḥudhayfa, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

Al-Tabarani related it with a weak chain from Umm Salama, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

There are hadiths traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer without mention of the day of the Confederates: among them from Ibn ʿUmar in Ibn Mandah; among them from Samura in Ahmad, Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani; among them also from him in Ibn Abi Shayba, Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and al-Tirmidhi, who authenticated it, and Ibn Jarir, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi authenticated it; and from Abu Hurayra in Ibn Jarir, al-Bayhaqi and al-Tahawi.

It was also related from him by Ibn Saʿid, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani; from Ibn ʿAbbas in al-Bazzar with sound chains; and from Abu Malik al-Ashʿari in Ibn Jarir and al-Tabarani. These are hadiths traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) explicitly stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer.

Great reports from the Companions also exist stating that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, and in what is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) there is what makes further evidence unnecessary.

As for what is related from ʿAli and Ibn ʿAbbas that they said: it is the Ṣubḥ prayer, as Malik related in the Muwatta' from them both; Ibn Jarir related it from Ibn ʿAbbas; likewise ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir related it from him; likewise Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Ibn ʿUmar; likewise Ibn Jarir related it from Jabir; likewise Ibn Abi Hatim related it from Abu Umama. All of these are from their own statements, and there is nothing among them traced to the Prophet (ﷺ). Such reports do not constitute proof, especially when they oppose what is established from him (ﷺ) with an establishment that can be claimed to be mass-transmitted (mutawatir). If the reports of the Companions do not constitute proof, then the reports of those after them, the Successors and their followers, are even less so.

Likewise, what Ibn Abi Hatim related with a good chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he said: the middle prayer is Maghrib, does not constitute proof. Likewise no weight is given to what came from a group of Companions that it is Zuhr or other prayers. Rather, what one who needs careful reflection should consider is what came traced to the Prophet (ﷺ) indicating that it is Zuhr, as Ibn Jarir related from Zayd ibn Thabit, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The middle prayer is the Ẓuhr prayer."

But its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is not sound; rather, what is related from Zayd ibn Thabit is his own statement. Evidence for this was drawn from the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to pray at al-hājira (midday), and it was the heaviest prayer for his Companions. But where does this argument stand against those sound, established hadiths from the Prophet (ﷺ)? Likewise, no weight is given to what is related from Ibn ʿUmar as his own statement that it is Zuhr.

The same applies to what is related from ʿAʾisha, Abu Saʿid al-Khudri and others. There is no proof in the statement of anyone against the statement of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

As for what ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Ibn Jarir and others related, that Ḥafṣa said to her freedman Abu Rafiʿ, when she had ordered him to write a Qur'an codex for her: "When you reach this verse, ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾, come to me so I may dictate it to you." When he reached it, she ordered him to write: "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer."

Malik, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan also related it from her, and they added: she said, "I bear witness that I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Malik, Ahmad, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and others related from Abu Yunus, the freedman of ʿAʾisha, that she ordered him to write a codex for her and said: "When you reach this verse, inform me: ﴿Guard the prayers and the middle prayer﴾." He said: "When I reached it, I informed her, and she dictated to me: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the ʿAṣr prayer.'" ʿAʾisha said: "I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Waki', Ibn Abi Shayba, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Umm Salama that she ordered someone to write a codex for her and told him what Ḥafṣa and ʿAʾisha had said.

The utmost that these reports from the three Mothers of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with them, establish is that they transmitted this wording in this way from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). There is nothing in them indicating that the middle prayer is Zuhr or otherwise. Rather, the most that the conjoining of the ʿAṣr prayer to the middle prayer indicates is that it is other than it, because the conjoined is other than that to which it is conjoined. This argument does not conflict with what is established from him (ﷺ) with an establishment that does not preclude that it is the ʿAṣr prayer, as we have already explained.

The conclusion: this reading transmitted by the three Mothers of the Believers, with the inclusion of "wa-ṣalāt al-ʿaṣr," is opposed by what Ibn Jarir related from ʿUrwa, who said: "In the codex of ʿAʾisha it was: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the ʿAṣr prayer.'"

Waki' related from Ḥumayda, who said: "I read in the codex of ʿAʾisha: 'Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr.'"

Ibn Abi Dawud related the same from Qabisa ibn Dhu'ayb.

Abu ʿUbayd, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Bukhari in his History, Ibn Jarir and al-Tahawi related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite it: "Guard the prayers and the middle prayer, the prayer of ʿAṣr."

Ibn Jarir reported from him concerning the verse, he said: "Every people of a religion stand in it disobedient; stand you in obedience."

Ibn Abi Shaybah reported from al-Dahhak something like it.

It is established in the two Sahihs and other works from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Indeed, in the prayer there is preoccupation." And in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, this prayer is not fit for anything of the speech of people; it is only glorification, magnification and recitation of the Qur'an."

The traditions have differed concerning the qunut that is agreed upon: whether it is before ruku' or after it, whether it is in all prayers or some of them, and whether it is specific to calamities (nawazil) or not. The preferred view is that it is specific to calamities.

We have explained this in our commentary on al-Muntaqa, so let him refer to it.

Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: "When there is close fighting, let him gesture with his head wherever his face is; this is His saying: ﴿فَرِجالًا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾."

'Abd ibn Humayd reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said concerning ﴿فَإنْ خِفْتُمْ فَرِجالًا أوْ رُكْبانًا﴾: "One rak'ah at a time."

Waki' and Ibn Jarir reported from Mujahid concerning ﴿فَإذا أمِنتُمْ﴾, he said: "You have left the abode of travel for the abode of residence."

This is a return to the rest of the rulings detailed earlier.

If the woman wished, she could remain in residence under the bequest, and if she wished, she could leave.

Ibn ʿAtiyya and al-Qadi ʿIyad reported that there is an ijmaʿ (scholarly consensus) that the one-year provision is abrogated and that her ʿidda is four months and ten days.

Al-Bukhari included in his Sahih what Ibn Jarir had reported from Mujahid.

It was also said that the khabar is His words, "for their wives." It was also said that the khabar is omitted: i.e., "the bequest of those who die is a bequest," or "the ruling concerning those who die is a bequest."

Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, and Ibn ʿAmir read it in the accusative (manṣub), on the basis of an omitted verb: i.e., "let them make a bequest (fa-l-yuwussu wasiyya)," or "God has bequeathed a bequest," or "God has prescribed upon them a bequest."

As for His words, "matāʿan" (provision). It is manṣub either as an object of "wasiyya," or by an omitted verb: i.e., "provide for them a provision," or "God has made that a provision for them." It is also permissible that it be manṣub as a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative).

Here, "matāʿ" means the provision of one year.

As for His words, "ghayra ikhrāj" (without expulsion), it is a ṣifa (qualifier) of "matāʿan." Al-Akhfash said it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as if he had said, "not expulsion (lā ikhrājan)." It was also said that it is a ḥāl, i.e., "provide for them while they are not expelled." It was also said that it is manṣub by removing the preposition: i.e., "without expulsion (min ghayri ikhrāj)." The meaning is that it is obligatory upon those who are dying to bequeath, before death comes upon them, for their wives that they be provided for after them for one full year, with maintenance and residence from their estate, and that they not leave their dwellings.

As for His words, "fa-in kharajna" (But if they leave), meaning by their own choice before the year ends, "fa-la junaha ʿalaykum" (then there is no blame upon you), i.e., there is no fault upon the guardian, the ruler, or others, "fīmā faʿalna fī anfusihinna" (for what they do with themselves), namely by exposing themselves to suitors and adorning themselves for them.

In this there is evidence that the women were given a choice regarding residence for the year, and that this was not a binding obligation upon them. It was also said that the meaning is "there is no blame upon you in cutting off maintenance from them," but this is weak, because the object of the blame has already been mentioned in the verse with His words, "for what they do."

It was said that it refers to the mutʿa (consolation gift), and that it is obligatory for every divorced woman. It was also said that this verse is specific to the thayyibāt (previously married women) who had been consummated, because the mutʿa for those with whom the husbands had not consummated the marriage had already been mentioned before this verse.

We have already discussed this mutʿa and the disagreement over whether it is specific to those divorced before consummation and the setting of a dowry, or is general to all divorced women. It was also said that this verse includes both the obligatory mutʿa, which is the mutʿa of a divorced woman before consummation and the setting of a dowry, and the non-obligatory mutʿa, which is the mutʿa of all other divorced women, for that is only recommended (mustaḥabb). He said: "O son of my brother, I do not change anything of it from its place."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the verse that he said: "The woman whose husband had died was given maintenance and residence in the house for a year. Then the verse of inheritance abrogated it, and a quarter or an eighth of what the husband left was made their share."

Ibn Jarir reported something similar from ʿAta'.

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also reported something similar from Ibn ʿAbbas by another route.

Al-Shafiʿi and ʿAbd al-Razzaq reported from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah that he said: "The woman whose husband has died has no maintenance; the inheritance is sufficient for her."

Abu Dawud, in his book on abrogation (Nasikh), and al-Nasa'i reported from ʿIkrima that he said: "It was abrogated by: 'Those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days' (﴿والَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنكم ويَذَرُونَ أزْواجًا يَتَرَبَّصْنَ بِأنْفُسِهِنَّ أرْبَعَةَ أشْهُرٍ وعَشْرًا﴾) [al-Baqara: 234]."

Ibn al-Anbari in al-Masahif reported something similar from Zayd ibn Aslam. He also reported something similar from Qatada.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Mujahid regarding His words, "fa-la junaha ʿalaykum fīmā faʿalna fī anfusihinna min maʿrūf" (there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an honourable manner), that he said: "Lawful, good marriage."

Ibn Jarir reported from Ibn Zayd that he said: "When the verse 'a provision in kindness, a duty upon the good-doers' (﴿مَتاعًا بِالمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلى المُحْسِنِينَ﴾) [al-Baqara: 236] was revealed, a man said: 'If I wish to do well, I will do it, and if I do not wish to do so, I will not do it.' So God revealed: 'And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing' (﴿ولِلْمُطَلَّقاتِ مَتاعٌ بِالمَعْرُوفِ حَقًّا عَلى المُتَّقِينَ﴾)."

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab that he said: "This verse was abrogated by His words: 'And if you divorce them before you have touched them, and you had already set a bridal portion for them, then half of what you have set' (﴿وإنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ وقَدْ فَرَضْتُمْ لَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةً فَنِصْفُ ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾) [al-Baqara: 237]."

He also reported from ʿAtta' ibn Khuṣayf regarding His words, "And for divorced women is a provision," that he said: "That was before the obligatory shares (farāʾiḍ)."

Malik, ʿAbd al-Razzaq, al-Shafiʿi, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi reported from Ibn ʿUmar that he said: "Every divorced woman has a mutʿa, except the one you divorce whom you have not consummated and for whom a dowry has been set; for her, half is sufficient as a provision."

Ibn al-Mundhir reported from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that he said: "Every believing woman who is divorced, whether free or a slave, has a mutʿa," and he recited, "And for divorced women is a provision in kindness, a duty upon the God-fearing."

Al-Bayhaqi reported from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah that he said: "When Hafs ibn al-Mughira divorced his wife Fatima, she came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to her husband: 'Provide for her.' He said: 'I do not have anything to provide for her with.' He said: 'There must be a provision. Provide for her, even if it is half a ṣāʿ of dates.'"

ʿAbd ibn Humayd reported from Abu al-ʿAliya regarding the verse that he said: "Every divorced woman has a mutʿa."

The interrogative here is for affirmation (taqrir), and the seeing mentioned is the seeing of the heart, not the seeing of the eye.

According to Sibawayh, the meaning is: "Pay attention to the matter of those who went out." It is said that this seeing does not need two objects.

The summary of this is that the seeing here, which means perception (idrak), is construed with the meaning of alerting (tanbih). It may also be construed with the meaning of reaching a limit (intiha'), that is: has your knowledge not reached them? Or with the meaning of arrival (wusul), that is: has your knowledge not arrived at them? It may also be the seeing of the eye, that is: have you not looked at those who went out?

God, glorified is He, made the story of these people, since it had such currency and fame, something that compels everyone to acknowledge it, as though it were known to every individual or visible to every observer. This is because the People of the Book had been informed of it, recorded it, and made its matter widely known. The address here is to everyone who is fit to receive it.

The speech runs in the manner of a proverb (mathal), in a context of wonder, claiming that it is so manifest and clear that the present and the absent alike perceive it equally.

His saying ﴿وهم أُلُوفٌ﴾ ("and they were thousands") is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "went out." "Uluf" is one of the plurals of multiplicity, which indicates that they were many thousands.

His saying ﴿حَذَرَ المَوْتِ﴾ ("fearing death") is an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu).

His saying ﴿فَقالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا﴾ ("So God said to them: Die") is a command of creation (amr takwin), an expression of the attachment of His will to their death all at once. Or it is an image (tamthil) of His causing them to die a single death, as though they were commanded and obeyed.

His saying ﴿ثُمَّ أحْياهُمْ﴾ ("Then He gave them life") is conjoined to an implied element required by the context. That is: God said to them, "Die," so they died, then He gave them life. Or it is conjoined to "He said," since "He said" was an expression for causing death.

His saying ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لَذُو فَضْلٍ عَلى النّاسِ﴾ ("Indeed God is full of bounty toward mankind"): the indefiniteness in His saying "bounty" is for magnification, that is: He is possessed of great bounty toward all of mankind. As for those who went out, it is because He gave them life so that they might take heed. As for the addressees, it is because He guided them to take heed and gain insight through the story of these people.

His saying ﴿وقاتِلُوا في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("And fight in the way of God") is conjoined to an implied element, as though it were said: "Give thanks for His bounty by taking heed of what He has related to you, and fight." This is so if the address in "and fight" refers back to the addressees in ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا﴾, as most of the exegetes (mufassirun) have said. On this view, the mention of this story serves to encourage the Muslims to strive (jihad). It has been said that the address is to those among the Children of Israel who were brought to life, in which case it is conjoined to His saying "Die," and there is an omission in the speech, its estimated sense being: "And He said to them: Fight."

Ibn Jarir said: There is no basis for the view of those who say that the command to fight was addressed to those who were brought back to life.

The lending to God is an image (mathal) for sending ahead a righteous deed for which its doer deserves reward. The original meaning of "qard" (loan) is a name for anything for which a recompense is sought. It is said: "Fulan lent Fulan," meaning he gave him something that would be repaid to him.

The poet said:

"And when you are repaid a loan, then repay it."

Al-Zajjaj said: In the language, "qard" means a good trial and an evil trial.

Umayya said:

"Every man will be repaid his loan, good or evil, and his debt in the measure that he paid."

Another said:

"He repaid the loans with their like: good with good, and evil with evil."

Al-Kisa'i said: "Qard" is what you have sent ahead of a righteous or evil deed. The root of the word is cutting, and from it comes "miqrad" (scissors). The calling for a loan in the verse is only for familiarization and bringing people near through what they can understand.

God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy. He likened the giving of the believer, whose reward in the Hereafter he seeks, to a loan, just as He likened the giving of souls and wealth in order to obtain Paradise to buying and selling.

His saying ﴿حَسَنًا﴾ ("good") means: one whose soul is content with it, without reproach or harm.

His saying ﴿فَيُضاعِفَهُ﴾ ("so that He may multiply it for him"): 'Asim and others read it with an alif and a fatha on the fa'.

Nafi', Abu 'Amr, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read it with the alif and a damma on the fa'. Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub read "fayudhA'ifahu" with the alif dropped, the 'ain doubled, and a fatha on the fa'. Ibn Kathir and Abu Ja'far read it with the doubling and a damma on the fa'.

There has been disagreement about the quantity of this multiplication, in several opinions.

It has been said: No one knows it except God alone.

His saying ﴿واللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ ويَبْسُطُ﴾ ("And God withholds and extends") is general over everything; He is the one who withholds and extends. "Qabd" is restriction, and "bast" is expansion. In it is a warning that whoever is stingy instead of extending will soon have it replaced by withholding. This is why He said: ﴿وإلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ ("and to Him you will be returned"), that is, He will recompense you for what you sent ahead when you return to Him. If you spend from what He has widened for you, He will do good to you; if you are stingy, He will punish you.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ﴾ ("Have you not seen those who went out of their homes"), that he said: They were four thousand who went out fleeing from the plague, and they said: "We will go to a land where there is no death." When they reached a certain place, God said to them: "Die," and they died. Then a prophet of the prophets passed by them and prayed to his Lord that He would give them life so that they might worship Him, and He gave them life.

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from him that the town they went out from was Dawardan.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted this story at length from Abu Malik, and in it they were thirty-some thousand.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz that their homes were Adhri'at.

He also transmitted from Abu Salih that they were nine thousand.

A group of the transmitting exegetes (muhaddithun mufassirun) related this story in various forms, and multiplying its chains brings no benefit.

It is related in the two Sahihs and others from the Prophet (ﷺ) the prohibition of fleeing from the plague, and of entering a land in which it is present, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf.

Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Sa'd, al-Bazzar, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا﴾ was revealed, Abu al-Dahdah al-Ansari said: 'O Messenger of God, does God indeed want a loan from us?' He said: 'Yes, O Abu al-Dahdah.' He said: 'Show me your hand, O Messenger of God.' So he gave him his hand. He said: 'Indeed, I have lent my orchard to my Lord, and He has in it six hundred palm trees.'"

'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Jarir transmitted this story through the route of Zayd ibn Aslam. Al-Tabarani added, from his father, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, and Ibn Mardawayh from Abu Hurayrah, and Ibn Ishaq and Ibn al-Mundhir from Ibn 'Abbas.

Ibn Jarir transmitted from al-Suddi regarding His saying ﴿أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ ("manifold multiples"), that he said: No one knows what this multiplication is.

Ahmad, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: A hadith reached me from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "Indeed God writes for His believing servant, for one good deed, a thousand thousand good deeds." So I performed the pilgrimage that year, and I had intended to make the pilgrimage only to meet him about this hadith. I met Abu Hurayrah and mentioned it to him. He said: "That is not what I said, and he did not memorize the hadith you were related. What I said was: 'Indeed God gives the believing servant, for one good deed, two thousand thousand good deeds.'" Then Abu Hurayrah said: "Do you not find this in the Book of God? ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾. So the 'many' with God is more than two thousand thousand and two thousand thousand. By Him in whose hand is my soul, I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: 'Indeed God multiplies the good deed two thousand thousand good deeds.'"

Then ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ أضْعافًا كَثِيرَةً﴾ was revealed. He said: 'My Lord, increase my community.' Then ﴿إنَّما يُوَفّى الصّابِرُونَ أجْرَهم بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾ [al-Zumar: 10] was revealed."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from Sufyan, who said: "When ﴿مَن جاءَ بِالحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أمْثالِها﴾ [al-An'am: 160] was revealed, he said: 'My Lord, increase my community.' Then ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾ was revealed; he said: 'My Lord, increase my community.' Then ﴿مَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أمْوالَهُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 261] was revealed; he said: 'My Lord, increase my community.' Then ﴿إنَّما يُوَفّى الصّابِرُونَ﴾ was revealed." There are other hadiths on this subject; these are the best of them, and they will come up at the commentary on His saying: ﴿كَمَثَلِ حَبَّةٍ أنْبَتَتْ سَبْعَ سَنابِلَ﴾, so investigate them there.

So He urged these to lend, saying: ﴿مَن ذا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾. He said: "He extends for you while you are heavy about going out and do not desire it, and He withholds from this one while he is glad in spirit to go out and is light about it. Another said:
